The targeted sub-region sampling is achieved by propagating manually defined subregions from a reference scan to the other >30,000 analyzed scans using image registration. The resulting collages can be compact while retaining high-resolution, for example by providing multiple slices of kidney tissue for a kidney volume regression network. This approach also enables group-wise saliency analysis that highlight image and anatomical regions used by the network for the pre- dictions. The method was applied for the regression endpoints of kidney volume, heart volume, and age. Predictive performance was found between R2 = 0.731-0.984 and the group-wise saliency maps were found to highlight medically relevant regions. We con- clude that the method can be used to standardize and restrict the information presented to a deep regression analysis pipeline, increasing information density and opening up a wide range of future medical inference studies.

items.title_en: OVM-Occ: Open-Vocabulary Monocular Occupancy Prediction via Geometry-Aware Vision-Language Distillation
items.abstract_en: Monocular occupancy prediction in indoor scenes aims to recover a scene's 3D geometry and semantics from a single RGB image. Existing methods are restricted to a closed set of predefined categories, limiting their ability to generalize to unseen categories. This limitation is particularly critical in indoor scenes, where objects exhibit highly diverse and fine-grained semantic categories. We study open-vocabulary monocular occupancy prediction for indoor scenes and present OVM-Occ, a Gaussian-based occupancy framework with an instance-aware vision-language teacher. Specifically, we adopt Language-Embedded Gaussians as the intermediate scene representation, propose a geometry-aware deformable attention module to refine Gaussian semantic features, and construct instance-level vision-language embeddings to provide reliable semantic supervision. We further introduce geometry-aware decoupled semantic distillation to mitigate the interference between geometry learning and semantic learning. To evaluate open-vocabulary occupancy prediction performance, we introduce OpenOcc-ScanNet and OpenOcc-Replica, two extended benchmarks with more diverse and fine-grained semantic categories. Experiments show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in open-vocabulary monocular occupancy prediction for indoor scenes, outperforming the previous state-of-the-art approach by 12.2 mIoU and 0.6 IoU on the Occ-ScanNet dataset, with consistent gains under new open-vocabulary evaluation protocols.

items.title_en: Low-rank MERA Decomposition of 3D OCT Image Volume for Compression, Denoising, Feature Extraction and Diagnosis of Retinal Diseases
items.title_zh: 用于视网膜疾病压缩、去噪、特征提取与诊断的3D OCT图像体数据低秩MERA分解
items.abstract_en: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is a non-invasive imaging modality used for visualization of retinal tissue. However, OCT volumes are affected by speckle noise, which degrades image contrast and obscures fine structural details. Furthermore, modern clinical practice requires large field-of-view, high-resolution OCT volumes, whose storage and transmission are demanding for archiving and teleophthalmology applications. To address aforementioned challenges, we propose a low-rank multi-scale entanglement renormalization ansatz (MERA) tensor network approximation of 3D OCT image volume, where the image volume is represented as contractions of a top core factor encoding global features and multiple interacting low-rank orthogonal or semi-orthogonal factors modeling inter- and intra-B scan correlations. This representation jointly enables compression, denoising, and feature extraction. Unlike deep learning approaches, the proposed approach is training-free and processes each OCT volume independently. We evaluate the proposed framework on OCT image volumes acquired by two different scanners and demonstrate improved visual quality and reduced retinal layer segmentation errors in comparison with several competing methods. We also extract MERA features from two clinical OCT volume datasets. They are subsequently classified using a Grassmann-manifold nearest-subspace classifier. With the subspace dimension as its only hyperparameter, the classifier is theoretically shown to be robust in small-sample clinical scenario. We demonstrate competitive accuracy of classification of retinal diseases in these small-sample settings, where deep learning methods are often limited by the scarcity of labeled data. The proposed structure-aware model-driven representation learning for high-dimensional data under limited supervision provides good generalization performance while maintaining high interpretability.

items.title_en: Beyond Vision-Language Models: Visual-Semantic Affect Graphs for Emotion Recognition in Artworks
items.abstract_en: Emotion recognition in artworks remains challenging because affective meaning is often subjective, implicit, and shaped by relationships between visual form and semantic associations. While vision-language models provide strong multimodal representations, direct image-to-emotion prediction may overlook explicit relations among formal, semantic, and affective cues that support emotional interpretation. This paper proposes Visual-Semantic Affect Graphs (VSAG), a graph-based framework that represents artworks through interpretable feature nodes, including color, brushstroke, composition, light-shadow, line quality, and extracted visual entities. The graph learns feature-emotion associations for dominant emotion prediction, with valence-arousal structure modeled through an optional hierarchical auxiliary affect module. We evaluate VSAG and VSAG-TopK against direct VLM inference using Qwen3-VL and InternVL3.5 on EmoArt-5k. Results show that direct VLMs provide useful but modest baselines, while graph-based models improve dominant emotion prediction. In particular, the hierarchical valence-arousal variant of VSAG achieves the best overall performance, improving accuracy, macro-F1, and weighted-F1 over both direct VLM inference and the emotion-only VSAG baseline. Per-class results indicate that graph-based models and VLMs capture partly complementary signals, while valence-arousal structure is most useful when integrated as a coarse-to-fine affect hierarchy rather than as a simple post-hoc correction. These findings suggest that explicit visual-semantic structure can support both prediction and interpretation in artwork emotion recognition.

items.title_en: Reading Beyond OCR Noise: Robust Cross-Lingual RAG for Legislative Archives
items.abstract_en: India's historical public archives present severe computer vision and document image analysis challenges: decades of parliamentary records survive only as degraded, multi-column scanned pages featuring mixed scripts, complex layouts, and dense visual noise where OCR failure is the primary obstacle to information retrieval. We present an end-to-end framework that couples vision-based layout segmentation and multi-script OCR with an agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline. Our approach specifically addresses how visual degradation and layout fragmentation propagate into text extraction errors, using an iterative agentic loop to navigate around OCR noise and layout ambiguities before generating answers. Evaluated on the 200,000-page Punjab Vidhan Sabha archive, our system demonstrates robust handling of historical document degradation, outperforming standard text-only baselines.

items.title_en: Thermal-Headroom Routing for Efficient Robot Perception in Extreme Heat
items.abstract_en: Adaptive robot perception systems must balance detector accuracy, inference latency, and energy consumption, particularly when high ambient temperatures cause processors to thermally throttle. We propose Thermal-Headroom Routing (THR), a lightweight model-selection policy that forecasts processor temperature using a closed-form RC thermal model and excludes detector configurations predicted to cross a throttling threshold. We evaluate THR with four YOLO11 configurations across seven real-world perception traces, eight ambient temperatures, and 20 randomized seeds, comparing it with latency-aware routing, fixed-threshold thermostats, duty caps, and a matched-compute-budget control. At ambient temperatures of 45-55 degrees C and a tight inference deadline, THR eliminates throttling in simulation, reduces deadline misses by 3.9-7.5 percentage points, and reduces energy per on-time frame by approximately 12-13% relative to a latency-belief router. A separate experiment using deadline-paced, nonoverlapping frame execution yields miss-rate reductions of 6.2-9.5 percentage points. A tuned thermostat or duty cap can match THR at a fixed operating point; predictive routing is most useful when ambient conditions or calibrated thermal parameters differ from those used to tune static policies. Measurements on an Apple M5 support the single-node heating approximation but do not validate hardware throttling. The results characterize the conditions under which thermal forecasting improves the efficiency and timeliness of resource-constrained robot perception.

items.title_en: Joint Latent Reasoning and Observation for Agentic Video Understanding
items.abstract_en: Effective video agents must learn not only how to answer, but also where to look next. Transferring this capability to smaller models is challenging because each observation serves two purposes: supporting an answer and guiding the search for further evidence. Textual descriptions may capture what is currently visible while omitting cues needed for subsequent acquisition. We introduce Latent Agentic Reasoning for Video Analysis (LARVA), a framework that distills multi-round video agents through jointly learned latent reasoning and visual observations. Rather than communicating through captions, an observer passes compact continuous representations to a reasoner that selects the next acquisition action or produces the final answer. Crucially, action and answer supervision propagate through this interface, training the observer to communicate information useful for downstream decisions. Observation reconstruction and reasoning-distribution alignment provide auxiliary supervision from textual teacher trajectories. Across five video-understanding benchmarks, LARVA achieves strong performance with 4B and 7B backbones. On VideoHolmes, Video-MME, and LVBench, the 7B model outperforms a textual CoT student trained on the same teacher trajectories by 5.1, 2.5, and 3.7 percentage points, respectively. These results highlight the value of jointly learning how agents represent evidence and act on it when distilling video-understanding capabilities.

items.title_en: GaussianSpline: Adaptive Bézier Splines for Highly Dynamic 4D Gaussian Splatting
items.abstract_en: We present GaussianSpline, a dynamic 4D Gaussian Splatting method that models per-Gaussian motion using adaptive, non-uniform piecewise cubic Bézier splines. Unlike approaches based on global deformations, fixed-order polynomials, or uniformly parameterized splines, GaussianSpline jointly learns the Bézier control points and the temporal partition of each Gaussian's trajectory. This adaptive representation allocates greater temporal capacity to highly dynamic regions while maintaining compact trajectories for near-static regions, enabling high-fidelity reconstruction of complex and rapidly changing motion. To jointly achieve globally smooth motion and local adaptivity, we enforce $G^1$ continuity between consecutive Bézier segments using a reflection-based constraint on their control points. This produces smooth, fully differentiable trajectories while preserving the flexibility of non-uniform temporal parameterization. Experiments on the Neural 3D Video benchmark, the Google Immersive dataset, as well as on synthetic scenes demonstrate that GaussianSpline substantially improves reconstruction quality in scenes with highly non-uniform and challenging dynamics, while maintaining competitive performance on general dynamic scenes compared with state-of-the-art 4D Gaussian Splatting methods.

items.title_en: O2D-MedNet: An Optimization-Aware Dual-Domain Framework for Robust Medical Image Segmentation
items.title_zh: O2D-MedNet：一种面向鲁棒医学图像分割的优化感知双域框架
items.abstract_en: Medical image segmentation (MIS) remains challenging due to composite degradations and multi-scale geometric variations, which jointly impair lesion-background separability, structural consistency, and optimization stability. Existing single-stream frameworks entangle heterogeneous cues within a single representation pathway, while hybrid-stream approaches often rely on generic or static fusion, limiting effective coordination across domains and failing to explicitly address optimization instability. To overcome these limitations, we propose a new optimization-aware dual-domain framework for MIS (O2D-MedNet). First, a degradation-aware dualdomain interaction (DDI) module integrates Fourier - and Wavelet-domain features to suppress degradation-sensitive responses while preserving structural and fine-detail information. Second, a cross-backbone contour-guided fusion (CGF) module enables selective interaction between CNN-based local detail modeling and visual state-space-based global structure modeling, improving boundary accuracy and representation consistency. Third, a gradient-context optimization (GCO) strategy stabilizes training by adaptively adjusting learning dynamics based on loss trends and gradient statistics, mitigating instability caused by class imbalance and heterogeneous sample difficulty. Extensive experiments on six benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art MIS methods across multiple imaging modalities. Further analyses confirm enhanced sensitivity, structural consistency, and optimization stability, validating the effectiveness of the proposed O2D-MedNet for robust MIS under heterogeneous conditions.

items.title_en: Multi-Agent Relay Thinking
items.abstract_en: Existing multi-agent collaboration (MAC) methods have primarily explored a group thinking collaboration topology, where agents independently generate solutions and aggregate their outputs. In this work, we investigate an alternative relay thinking topology, where reasoning ownership is dynamically transferred across agents, allowing subsequent agents to inherit and refine an evolving reasoning trajectory. We introduce Multi-Agent Confidence-guided Relay (MACR), a framework that enables dynamical relay collaboration among agents. The key challenge is determining when reasoning should be relayed and which agent should continue the process. method addresses this challenge through confidence-guided relay triggering and a bidding mechanism that selects the next agent based on its confidence. Experiments on four benchmarks show that method outperforms the strongest single-model strategies in accuracy, e.g., +3.3% on MathVista and +3.9% on MMStar, and remains on par with multi-agent strategies while consuming 6.0x less token overhead on HallusionBench and MMStar.Further analysis demonstrates that relay collaboration enables heterogeneous agents to progressively integrate complementary insights, combining heterogeneous capabilities across reasoning stages. Our source code is available at https://github.com/67L1/MACR.

items.title_en: At last, an explicit singular value decomposition for electrical impedance tomography
items.abstract_en: We derive a diagonalization of the normal operator of the linearized electrical impedance tomography (EIT) problem on the disk in the case of a radially symmetric Schrödinger potential with Dirichlet-to-Neumann data. The diagonalization is achieved by transforming the normal operator to the adjacent interval finite Hilbert transform which has a known spectral theory including a commuting differential operator. The normal operator in this case is not compact and the spectrum continuous.

items.title_en: OrthoRF: Exploring Orthogonality in Object-Centric Representations
items.abstract_en: Neural synchrony is hypothesized to help the brain organize visual scenes into structured multi-object representations. In machine learning, synchrony-based models analogously learn object-centric representations by storing binding in the phase of complex-valued features. Rotating Features (RF) instantiate this idea with vector-valued activations, encoding object presence in magnitudes and affiliation in orientations. We propose Orthogonal Rotating Features (OrthoRF), which enforces orthogonality in RF's orientation space via an inner-product loss and architectural modifications. This yields sharper phase alignment and more reliable grouping. In evaluations of unsupervised object discovery, including settings with overlapping objects, noise, and out-of-distribution tests, OrthoRF matches or outperforms current models while producing more interpretable representations, and it eliminates the post-hoc clustering required by many synchrony-based approaches. Unlike current models, OrthoRF also recovers occluded object parts, indicating stronger grouping under occlusion. Overall, orthogonality emerges as a simple, effective inductive bias for synchrony-based object-centric learning.

items.title_en: Gold nanorods targeting tumor vasculature: Monte Carlo evaluation of the radioenhancement effects
items.abstract_en: Gold nanoparticles targeted to tumor vasculature can raise the dose to endothelial cells, and the enhancement depends on their position relative to the vessel wall. Despite growing interest in endothelial radiosensitization, intravascular and immediate perivascular dose enhancement has not been resolved at the level of individual endothelial cells for different nanoparticle locations. Earlier vascular dosimetry scored thin wall layers, analytic endothelial slabs, or tissue-region averages. This study quantifies the dose enhancement ratio (DER) of gold nanorods (AuNRs) in individual endothelial cells and in the perivascular region for three AuNR locations. Track-structure Monte Carlo simulations in TOPAS modeled a 10 um long, 16 um diameter microvessel segmented into six endothelial cells. AuNRs were placed homogeneously in the lumen, on the inner vessel wall (vascular-targeted), or on the outer vessel wall (extravasated) at concentrations of 5 to 50 mg Au/g water within the vessel volume under 50 and 100 kVp X-rays. All DERs were corrected for the lack of charged-particle equilibrium (CPE) inherent to microscale simulations. Inner wall-attached AuNRs produced the highest microvessel-averaged DERs, reaching approximately 3.8 at 50 mg Au/g water and approximately 1.96 at 18 mg Au/g water under 50 kVp. The DER increased linearly with AuNR concentration and was higher at 50 kVp than at 100 kVp. Including AuNRs outside the simulated segment (infinite vessel approximation) increased endothelial DERs by 5 to 10 percent. In the perivascular region, the DER was highest within the first 10 um, where outer wall-attached AuNRs gave the highest values. The results establish a physical dose enhancement basis for endothelial and perivascular cells and can guide the design of vascular-targeted radiosensitization.

items.title_en: Ms4a4a loss preferentially remodels microglia with limited, compartment-specific effects across central and peripheral immune compartments in 5xFAD mice
items.title_zh: Ms4a4a 缺失优先重塑小胶质细胞，并在 5xFAD 小鼠中枢与外周免疫区室中产生有限且区室特异的影响
items.abstract_en: Background: Genome-wide association studies have identified the MS4A locus as a major modifier of Alzheimers disease (AD) risk and resilience. MS4A4A is enriched in microglia, and we previously demonstrated that loss of Ms4a4a reduces amyloid plaque pathology and attenuates amyloid-associated tau spreading. However, MS4A4A is also expressed in peripheral myeloid populations, raising the possibility that its effects extend beyond brain-resident microglia. Here, we sought to define how constitutive Ms4a4a loss alters immune populations across central nervous system (CNS), CNS-border, and peripheral compartments in the context of amyloid pathology. Methods: We performed multicompartment immune profiling by flow cytometry in 5xFAD Ms4a4a wild-type and 5xFAD Ms4a4a-deficient mice. Myeloid and lymphoid populations were characterized in the brain, dural meninges, skull bone marrow, tibial bone marrow, and spleen. Results: Ms4a4a loss produced its strongest immune effects in brain microglia. 5xFAD Ms4a4a-deficient mice exhibited increased microglial abundance, increased frequency and expression of CD86, increased MHC class II expression intensity, and enrichment of CXCR4-high microglia, whereas P2RY12 and TREM2 were unchanged. Brain macrophages showed increased MHC class II expression, whereas conventional dendritic cells (cDCs) in the brain showed reduced MHC class II expression, with limited changes in other infiltrating immune populations. Immune composition in the dura and skull bone marrow was largely preserved, although MHC class II expression was increased in skull bone marrow cDCs. Peripheral immune composition in tibial bone marrow and spleen was similarly preserved, with selective increases in M2-like macrophages in tibial bone marrow and splenic CD8 T-cell frequency. Conclusions: These findings identify microglia as the immune population most strongly remodeled by Ms4a4a loss in the setting of amyloid pathology. Constitutive Ms4a4a deficiency does not produce broad systemic immune remodeling but instead preferentially alters microglial state, accompanied by more limited, cell type- and tissue-specific effects across other central and peripheral immune compartments. These findings establish MS4A4A as a context-dependent regulator of immune responses to AD pathology with particularly prominent effects on microglia.
items.abstract_zh: 背景：全基因组关联研究提示 MS4A 位点是阿尔茨海默病（AD）风险和韧性的重要修饰因子。MS4A4A 富集于小胶质细胞，既往研究表明 Ms4a4a 缺失可减少淀粉样斑块病理并减弱淀粉样蛋白相关 tau 播散。但 MS4A4A 也表达于外周髓系细胞，其作用可能不限于脑内小胶质细胞。方法：研究用流式细胞术对 5xFAD Ms4a4a 野生型和缺陷型小鼠进行多区室免疫 profiling，分析脑、硬脑膜、颅骨骨髓、胫骨骨髓和脾中的髓系与淋系细胞。结果：Ms4a4a 缺失的免疫效应在脑小胶质细胞中最强，缺陷小鼠小胶质细胞数量增加、CD86 频率和表达升高、MHC II 表达强度增加、CXCR4-high 小胶质细胞富集，而 P2RY12 和 TREM2 不变。脑巨噬细胞 MHC II 升高，而脑常规树突状细胞（cDCs）MHC II 降低，其他浸润免疫细胞变化有限。硬脑膜和颅骨骨髓免疫组成基本保留，但颅骨骨髓 cDCs 的 MHC II 升高。胫骨骨髓和脾的外周免疫组成同样基本保留，仅胫骨骨髓 M2 样巨噬细胞和脾 CD8 T 细胞频率选择性增加。
items.highlight_zh: Ms4a4a 缺失主要重塑脑小胶质细胞，外周免疫改变有限
items.digest_zh: 本研究要回答：在淀粉样病理背景下，组成性 Ms4a4a 缺失究竟如何影响中枢神经系统、CNS 边界以及外周免疫区室，而不只是脑内小胶质细胞。作者采用 5xFAD 阿尔茨海默病模型小鼠，比较 Ms4a4a 野生型与缺陷型，并用流式细胞术系统分析脑、硬脑膜、颅骨骨髓、胫骨骨髓和脾中的髓系与淋系免疫群体。结果显示，效应最强的是脑小胶质细胞：缺陷小鼠小胶质细胞增多，CD86 和 MHC II 表达增强，CXCR4-high 群体富集，而 P2RY12、TREM2 未变；脑巨噬细胞 MHC II 升高，但脑 cDCs 的 MHC II 反而降低。硬脑膜、颅骨骨髓、胫骨骨髓和脾整体免疫组成基本保持，仅有颅骨骨髓 cDCs MHC II 升高、胫骨骨髓 M2 样巨噬细胞增多和脾 CD8 T 细胞频率增加等选择性变化。该工作说明 Ms4a4a 缺失的作用以脑小胶质细胞为中心，外周影响有限且具区室特异性，为将 MS4A4A 作为 AD 靶点提供了免疫学依据，也提示需关注不同免疫区室的差异。

items.title_en: Early clonal dominance at priming sets the trajectory for broad HIV serum neutralization
items.title_zh: 免疫启动阶段的早期克隆优势决定广谱 HIV 血清中和轨迹
items.abstract_en: Germline-targeting vaccines aim to elicit HIV-1 broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs), but determinants of serum bnAb induction remain unclear. We previously showed that Q23-APEX-GT2 primes diverse V2-apex bnAb precursors in outbred rhesus macaques (RMs). To assess their maturation into authentic bnAbs, we infected immunized RMs with CAP256.SU SHIV. Four of six developed heterologous serum neutralization breadth, with one neutralizing ~70% of viruses tested. Early autologous neutralization and B-cell priming efficiency post-prime correlated with post-infection breadth. Longitudinal lineage tracing in lymph-nodes and blood revealed that recruitment and expansion of diverse long-CDRH3 V2-apex B-cell precursors, followed by early dominance of one or two clones, predicted serum breadth. Structural analyses showed that non-neutralizing lineages failed despite cross-reactive Env binding, owing to unfavorable V2-apex approach angles and limited glycan engagement. Together, these findings identify priming efficiency and early clonal dominance as key determinants of serum bnAb induction and provide a framework for HIV vaccine design.
items.abstract_zh: 生殖系靶向疫苗旨在诱导 HIV-1 广谱中和抗体（bnAbs），但血清 bnAb 诱导的决定因素仍不清楚。作者此前发现 Q23-APEX-GT2 可在远交恒河猴中启动多样的 V2-apex bnAb 前体。为评估其成熟为真正 bnAb 的能力，研究者用 CAP256.SU SHIV 感染免疫猴。6 只中有 4 只产生异源血清中和广度，其中 1 只中和约 70% 受试病毒。免疫后早期自体中和及 B 细胞启动效率与感染后广度相关。淋巴结和血液的纵向谱系追踪显示，多样长 CDRH3 V2-apex B 细胞前体的招募和扩增，随后一两个克隆的早期优势可预测血清广度。结构分析表明，非中和谱系虽能交叉反应性结合 Env，却因 V2-apex 接近角度不利和聚糖参与有限而失败。研究将启动效率和早期克隆优势确定为血清 bnAb 诱导的关键决定因素，并为 HIV 疫苗设计提供框架。
items.highlight_zh: 启动效率与早期克隆优势决定 HIV 广谱中和
items.digest_zh: 这篇论文关注 HIV 疫苗中的一个核心难题：即使疫苗能启动广谱中和抗体前体，为什么最终只有部分个体产生广谱血清中和？作者利用此前建立的 Q23-APEX-GT2 生殖系靶向免疫方案，在远交恒河猴中先启动多样的 V2-apex 广谱中和抗体前体，再用 CAP256.SU SHIV 感染来检验这些前体能否成熟为真正 bnAb。结果显示，6 只免疫猴中 4 只出现异源血清中和广度，1 只可中和约 70% 的测试病毒。关键预测因素不是单一抗体特性，而是免疫后 B 细胞启动效率、早期自体中和，以及淋巴结和血液中长 CDRH3 V2-apex 前体的招募扩增后一两个克隆的早期优势。结构分析进一步解释失败谱系：它们虽能交叉反应结合 Env，但因 V2-apex 接近角度不佳、聚糖接触有限而未能中和。该研究把“启动质量”和“早期克隆竞争”联系起来，为设计能引导 bnAb 成熟轨迹的 HIV 疫苗提供了可检验框架。

items.title_en: Weaning imprints a hybrid cytotoxic-regulatory identity on intestinal CD4+ T lymphocytes
items.title_zh: 断奶赋予肠道 CD4+ T 淋巴细胞细胞毒性-调节性混合身份
items.abstract_en: The intestinal immune system must adapt as the neonatal gut shifts from milk to solid food and becomes densely colonized. How the T cell compartment is established under these conditions remains unclear. Using fate-mapping to timestamp naive T cells, with imaging, transcriptomic, and repertoire analyses, we tracked them from suckling to adulthood. Intestinal T cell entry peaked at weaning, coinciding with relocation from crypts to villi guided by the tissue microenvironment and, partly, the microbiota. T cells timestamped at suckling persisted into adulthood and, at weaning, adopted a transient cytotoxic-regulatory state in the lamina propria, with granzyme B expression microbiota-dependent only in the ileum. Clonal expansions at weaning were restricted to the small intestinal lamina propria and absent in germ-free mice. Most expanded clones recognized early-life commensals. Weaning is a physiological window of transient inflammation imprinting a hybrid CD4 T cell compartment, suggesting that early-life commensals modulate T cell selection.
items.abstract_zh: 新生儿肠道从母乳转向固体食物并逐渐被密集定植，肠道免疫系统必须随之适应。T 细胞区室在此条件下如何建立仍不清楚。作者用命运图谱给初始 T 细胞打时间戳，并结合成像、转录组和库分析，从哺乳期追踪到成年。肠道 T 细胞进入在断奶期达到峰值，恰逢其受组织微环境及部分微生物群引导从隐窝迁往绒毛。哺乳期标记的 T 细胞可持续到成年，并在断奶时于固有层获得短暂的细胞毒性-调节性状态，其中颗粒酶 B 表达仅在回肠依赖微生物群。断奶期克隆扩增局限于小肠固有层，在无菌小鼠中缺失。多数扩增克隆识别早期共生菌。断奶是短暂炎症的生理窗口，铭刻出混合型 CD4 T 细胞区室，提示早期共生菌可调节 T 细胞选择。
items.highlight_zh: 断奶期短暂炎症塑造肠道 CD4 T 细胞混合身份
items.digest_zh: 研究问题是：新生儿肠道从吃奶转为固体食物、并被微生物密集定植时，肠道 CD4+ T 细胞区室是如何建立和塑形的。作者用 fate-mapping 给初始 T 细胞打“时间戳”，再结合成像、转录组和 T 细胞受体库分析，从哺乳期一直追踪到成年。结果发现，T 细胞进入肠道的高峰恰在断奶期，并伴随它们从隐窝向绒毛迁移，这一过程受组织微环境引导，也部分依赖微生物群。哺乳期被标记的 T 细胞能长期存留至成年，并在断奶时于固有层进入一种短暂的细胞毒性-调节性混合状态；颗粒酶 B 的表达只在回肠依赖微生物群。断奶期的克隆扩增局限在小肠固有层，无菌小鼠中不存在，且多数扩增克隆识别早期共生菌。该研究把断奶视为一个生理性短暂炎症窗口，说明早期微生物暴露会塑造肠道 T 细胞选择与身份，对理解生命早期免疫教育、疫苗和黏膜免疫具有重要意义。

items.title_en: Divide and conquer: a viral bifunctional RNA utilizes both RNA and protein to modulate pro-tumourigenic pathways
items.title_zh: 分而治之：一种病毒双功能RNA利用RNA和蛋白质调控促肿瘤途径
items.abstract_en: Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) is an oncogenic herpesvirus that causes the endothelial cell neoplasm Kaposi's sarcoma (KS) and other B-cell malignancies. The viral transcript kaposin is largely composed of GC-rich direct repeats (DRs) and is expressed during all phases of KSHV replication. Kaposin is polycistronic, encoding for at least 3 kaposin (Kap) proteins; of these, KapB is the most abundant and well-studied. Recent work from our lab discovered that kaposin is found in nuclear speckles (NSs) and that DRs are required for NS retention. During latency, kaposin is predominantly in NSs and is not exported or translated into KapB. During viral reactivation, abundant kaposin correlates with kaposin escape from NSs and KapB protein production. Thus, although kaposin is a latent transcript, KapB protein production occurs only during lytic reactivation. The spatiotemporal regulation of kaposin translation by NS retention during KSHV latency likewise suggests that these two biomolecules may have distinct functions. Because historically kaposin was viewed as a protein-coding mRNA, overexpression studies attributed any function to KapB even though both kaposin and KapB were produced in these systems. Armed with the knowledge that kaposin is a bifunctional RNA which derives function from both the transcript and the protein(s) it encodes, it remains unclear whether prior phenotypes should be attributed to kaposin or KapB. In this study, we developed a reductionist overexpression system to uncouple the effects of these biomolecules. To mimic kaposin during viral latency, we used a construct capable of forming kaposin NSs that does not translate reported Kap proteins ({Delta}Starts). To mimic late lytic reactivation, we used a recoded construct, AltB, that does not form kaposin NSs, is readily exported from the nucleus, and translates abundant KapB. We found that KapB protein induced actin stress fibre formation, cell enlargement, increased total levels of Yes-associated protein (YAP) and increased YAP-target gene transcription including pro-growth and pro-inflammatory transcripts. Conversely, kaposin RNA induced cell autonomous p-body disassembly with an overall reduction in pro-growth and pro-inflammatory transcripts, suggesting kaposin might sustain cell survival while dampening immune signalling. Taken together, we demonstrate that kaposin RNA and KapB protein have distinct and sometimes opposing effects on cellular growth and inflammatory signalling pathways, highlighting the ability of a viral bifunctional RNA to use both its RNA and protein products to mediate viral tumourigenesis.

items.title_en: The self-sufficient Aspergillus fumigatus Δ9-fatty acid desaturase SdeA requires a fused cytochrome b5 domain and hinge-dependent self-association for virulence
items.title_zh: 自足的烟曲霉Δ9-脂肪酸去饱和酶SdeA需要融合的细胞色素b5结构域和铰链依赖的自缔合来维持毒力
items.abstract_en: Fungal {Delta}9-fatty acid desaturases are self-sufficient enzymes in which the electron-donating cytochrome b5 (Cytb5) module is fused to the catalytic core, yet whether this covalent linkage is architecturally required has remained untested. Here we show that in the human pathogen Aspergillus fumigatus the Cytb5 module of the {Delta}9-desaturase SdeA must act in cis, within a self-associated complex organized by a hinge segment. AlphaFold3 modeling predicts a dimer in which the Cytb5 domain of one protomer approaches the other's di-iron center at a distance compatible with electron tunneling, and reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation shows that full-length SdeA self-associates in vivo. The recombinant Cytb5 module displays the spectral signatures of a genuine heme-binding redox domain. Nevertheless, deleting the Cytb5 domain, substituting its heme-coordinating histidines, or removing the 25-residue hinge each abolishes growth and virulence in Galleria mellonella without disrupting endoplasmic reticulum targeting, and a detached Cytb5-containing segment does not restore function. Hinge deletion abolishes stable SdeA self-association, identifying this segment as a structural organizer of the catalytically competent complex. Finally, we find no evidence that the sdeB locus provides a backup {Delta}9-desaturase. These results define the architectural requirements of a self-sufficient fungal desaturase and identify vulnerabilities absent from the human {Delta}9-desaturase for antifungal targeting.

items.title_en: A direct RPA-Polθ interaction licenses theta-mediated end joining
items.title_zh: 直接的RPA-Polθ相互作用许可θ介导的末端连接
items.abstract_en: DNA double-strand break repair often involves end resection, yet how resected ends are directed toward distinct repair pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we identify replication protein A (RPA) as an unexpected essential factor for cellular polymerase theta-mediated end joining (TMEJ). Using MUSIC-MAP, a newly developed platform linking endogenous sequence variants to DNA repair outcomes, we map a discrete functional interface between RPA2 and polymerase theta (Pol{theta}). Disrupting this interface in RPA2 abolishes TMEJ without impairing cell viability or homologous recombination. Mutations in the complementary Pol{theta} surface likewise impair TMEJ, whereas reciprocal charge-reversal mutations in RPA2 and Pol{theta} restore TMEJ, providing genetic evidence for a direct physical interaction. Structural modeling suggests that the Pol{theta}-binding surface becomes accessible at RPA-coated ssDNA termini, positioning RPA as a docking platform for Pol{theta} engagement. These findings reveal how RPA, previously considered a barrier to TMEJ, instead functions as a molecular platform that translates the organization of ssDNA into selective enzyme engagement, enabling mutagenic repair without compromising homologous recombination.

items.title_en: Structural Modeling Identifies a Conserved ADAR1 dsRBDIII Motif Predicted to Interact with PKR at Thr451
items.title_zh: 结构建模鉴定出一个保守的ADAR1 dsRBDIII基序，其被预测在Thr451处与PKR相互作用
items.abstract_en: Protein kinase R (PKR) is a key cellular dsRNA sensor whose activation is regulated by ADAR1. Although ADAR1 PKR association is established, its molecular determinants remain poorly understood. Molecular docking identified a conserved W768/F769/P770 (WFP) motif within ADAR1 dsRBD III as a potential PKR interaction interface. Disruption of this motif altered the predicted binding configuration. However, coimmunoprecipitation revealed no significant reduction in PKR association following individual substitutions or deletion of the WFP motif, although the deletion showed a consistent trend toward reduced binding. RNase treatment reduced PKR coimmunoprecipitation approximately tenfold without abolishing the interaction. These findings suggest that ADAR1 PKR association is predominantly RNA dependent, potentially involving shared dsRNA substrates that facilitate direct protein protein contacts, with the WFP motif contributing to interaction stability.

items.title_en: Roles of Neuromedin-U and Endothelin-1 in human cardiac organoid differentiation
items.title_zh: Neuromedin-U和Endothelin-1在人心脏类器官分化中的作用
items.abstract_en: During recent years, many new culture methods have been established to generate cardiomyocytes, using signaling and patterning factors that play important roles in mammalian heart development. Here, we identify two additional pathways of interest using a cardiac differentiation roadmap that we have generated, involving the endothelin 1 receptor EDNRA gene, and the Neuromedin family signaling peptide gene NMU. Treatment with NMU had most effect in ventricular lineages where it normally is not abundantly expressed, leading to a significant shift from ventricular cardiomyocyte (vCM) differentiation to non-myocytes, as shown with reporters and cell type-specific markers, which was associated with an increased beating frequency. This was not observed in atrial cultures. Treating atrial cultures with endothelin 1 (ET-1, EDN1) increased the number of atrial cardiomyocytes (aCM), while reducing repolarization times, increasing the contraction frequencies and altering the patterns of action potential propagations across the tissue. In ventricular cultures, a reduction in ventricular cardiomyocyte (vCM) numbers was observed, suggesting a combinatorial effect of ET-1 and retinoic acid (RA) on cardiomyocyte differentiation. These results identify ET-1 and NMU as important signaling factors for cardiomyocyte differentiation and electrophysiology of cardiac organoids, with ET-1 enhancing aCM differentiation when added around the time of posteriorization of the second heart field. NMU added without RA reduces the number of vCMs in the culture while it changes the organoids to exhibit a more atrial-like beating frequency.

items.title_en: An improved CRISPR-LICHT screen of 120 Tdark genes illuminates new biologically relevant SOX2 targets in human brain organoids
items.title_zh: 对120个Tdark基因的改进CRISPR-LICHT筛选揭示了人脑类器官中新的生物学相关SOX2靶点
items.abstract_en: SOX2 is a transcription factor and central regulator of neural progenitor identity, yet the downstream molecular networks through which it supports human brain development remain incompletely characterized. Here, we applied CRISPR-lineage tracing at cellular resolution in heterogeneous tissue (CRISPR-LICHT) to human cerebral organoids to functionally interrogate SOX2-dependent regulatory networks. Using a SOX2-focused library targeting SOX2 together with conserved neurodevelopmental regulators expressed in neural progenitor cells, we showed that CRISPR-LICHT detects reproducible lineage- depletion phenotypes across genes already known to be involved in progenitor maintenance, fate specification, glial differentiation and neuronal maturation. This extends the application of CRISPR-LICHT beyond the severe neural progenitor phenotypes previously characterized for microcephaly-associated genes and demonstrates its ability to detect perturbation effects across a broader set of neurodevelopmental regulators, involving SOX2 targets previously defined in mouse and now open to further understanding in a human model setting. We further screened 120 evolutionarily conserved, poorly characterized SOX2-dependent genes classified as Tdark within the Illuminating the Druggable Genome framework and identified 28 candidate hits whose disruption impaired neural progenitor lineage expansion and/or survival. These candidates included proteins associated with cytoskeletal organization, membrane dynamics and intracellular architecture, suggesting that SOX2-dependent developmental programmes may engage cellular processes beyond transcriptional regulation. Individual downregulation of CDC42EP4, a poorly characterized CDC42 effector linked to cytoskeletal organization, revealed altered distribution of targeted progenitors between ventricular- and subventricular- like compartments, with changes consistent with altered progenitor-state progression. Together, these findings expand the functional landscape of SOX2-dependent regulation in human neural progenitors and identify cellular architecture as a potential component of SOX2-associated developmental programs.

items.title_en: Vascular specification from diversified mesoderm culminates in endothelial convergence
items.title_zh: 多样化中胚层的血管特化最终导致内皮汇聚
items.abstract_en: Vasculogenesis establishes the embryonic circulatory system, yet how a common vascular program emerges across multiple embryonic and extraembryonic developmental environments remains incompletely understood. Here, we reconstruct mouse vasculogenesis through integrated single-cell, spatial, lineage and perturbation analyses. We find that vascular specification emerges from distinct sources of pre-specified mesoderm through a transient Kdr+Etv2- vascular-primed state promoted by BMP signaling. Primed cells persist until E8.0- E8.5, after which they resolve into committed derivatives. Dual blood-endothelial potential is largely restricted to early vitelline progenitors, whereas embryonic and umbilical progenitors contribute predominantly to endothelial lineages. Temporal VEGF signaling perturbations validate the inferred specification sequence, placing VEGF downstream of vascular priming and demonstrating its indispensable role in vascular and primitive blood specification. Unlike most developmental lineages, endothelial derivatives converge toward a common transcriptional state while retaining transcriptional traces of their developmental origins. Together, these findings establish a mechanistically validated developmental sequence for mammalian vasculogenesis.

items.title_en: Host genetics structure Symbiodiniaceae and prokaryotic assemblages and their co-variation in sympatric fire coral species
items.title_zh: 宿主遗传结构塑造Symbiodiniaceae与原核生物群落及其在同域火珊瑚物种中的共变异
items.abstract_en: Host genetic and environmental filtering are key determinants of microbiome assembly, yet their relative influence across multiple symbiotic compartments remains poorly understood. In coral holobionts, studies typically focus on either algal or bacterial symbionts and rarely account for host genetic variation below the species level. Here, we combined host microsatellite genotyping with ITS2 and 16S rRNA metabarcoding to investigate the drivers of Symbiodiniaceae and prokaryotic assemblages in three sympatric fire coral species (Millepora cf. exaesa, M. tenera, and M. cf. platyphylla) across three adjacent but environmentally contrasting reef habitats on Reunion Island. Both symbiont assemblages were structured by host identity and habitat, although host genetics consistently outweighed environmental effects on the microbiome composition. At the subspecies level, host genotypes explained up to 54% of the variation in Symbiodiniaceae assemblages compared to 20% for the prokaryotes. Symbiodiniaceae communities were dominated by Symbiodinium A16 and A3 radiations, while showing marked specificity across species and habitats. All Millepora species consistently associated with the Spirochaetaceae, Kiloniellaceae and Desulfobacteraceae bacterial families across all habitats, suggesting evolutionarily maintained core associations. Integrative analysis further demonstrated genotype-specific co-variation between algal and bacterial symbionts, with some genotypes maintaining stable and co-varying symbionts across clones, while others exhibited more flexible assemblages. Together, our results indicate that sympatric fire coral acquire symbionts from locally available pools through host genotype-dependent filtering. This study highlights host genotype as a major determinant of coral holobiont assembly, shaping the composition and co-variation of both Symbiodiniaceae and prokaryotic assemblages.

items.title_en: Hepatocyte nuclear factor-1β recruits the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase complex to activate gene transcription
items.title_zh: 肝细胞核因子-1β招募核小体重塑和去乙酰化酶复合物来激活基因转录
items.abstract_en: Mutations affecting the transcription factor hepatocyte nuclear factor-1{beta} (HNF-1{beta}) are the most common monogenic cause of congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract. The mechanism whereby HNF-1{beta} regulates gene transcription remains unclear. Here, we performed an unbiased proteomic screen and found that endogenous HNF-1{beta} interacts with core subunits of the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase complex (NuRD) in renal epithelial cells. Genome-wide ChIP-seq studies demonstrated colocalization of endogenous HNF-1{beta} and the core NuRD subunits GATAD2A, CHD4, and MBD3 at 2,776 primarily intergenic and intronic sites in native chromatin from wild-type renal epithelial cells. NuRD co-occupancy at 628 of the sites (22.6%) was reduced in the absence of HNF-1{beta}. Of the 628 HNF-1{beta}-dependent NuRD-occupied sites, 113 sites (18.2%) showed higher ATAC-seq peaks, indicative of open chromatin, and enrichment of histone H3 lysine-27 (H3K27) acetylation, indicative of active enhancers, in wild-type cells compared to HNF-1{beta}-deficient cells. Correlation with transcriptomic profiles in wild-type and HNF-1{beta}-deficient cells revealed that most of the sites were located near genes that are activated by HNF-1{beta}. Knockdown of CHD4 with shRNA resulted in decreased expression of 67 HNF-1{beta}-regulated genes that contained nearby NuRD and HNF-1{beta} co-occupied sites. Collectively, these results demonstrate that HNF-1{beta} recruits the NuRD complex resulting in H3K27 acetylation and chromatin opening and leading to gene activation. Our findings reveal a new mechanism of HNF-1{beta}-dependent gene expression and expand the role of the NuRD complex in gene activation at distal enhancers.

items.title_en: Excluded Volume Effect-induced Shrinkage for Resolution Enhancement of Hydrogel Bioconstructs
items.title_zh: 排除体积效应诱导的收缩用于增强水凝胶生物构建体的分辨率
items.abstract_en: Biofabrication of hydrogel materials is usually constrained by process-specific resolution limits. Here, we introduce excluded volume effect-induced shrinkage (EVER), a dehydration-enabled resolution enhancement strategy that achieves dimensional refinement via post-processing. In this approach, we treat biofabricated constructs with hydrophilic macromolecular crowding agent bath, with poloxamer as a representative. With EVER treatment, gelatin-based constructs can reach a dimension reduction of up to ~49% with an estimated volumetric reduction of ~87%. Shape fidelity was well retained after shrinkage across different constructs and could be stabilized by introducing secondary crosslinking. In extrusion bioprinted cell-laden constructs, myoblasts retained a considerable cell viability right after the shrinkage treatment and recovered significantly by day 1, with subsequent cell spreading and increasing proliferation over 7 days. Without the need of continued immersion in the shrinkage bath, EVER provides a hardware-independent route for refining hydrogel structures while retaining encapsulated cell compatibility.

items.title_en: MPFIL: Multi-Level Protein Feature Integration for Predicting Mutation-Induced Protein-Protein Binding Affinity Changes
items.title_zh: MPFIL：多层级蛋白质特征整合用于预测突变诱导的蛋白质-蛋白质结合亲和力变化
items.abstract_en: Predicting mutation-induced changes in protein protein binding affinity ({triangleup}{triangleup}G) is challenging because mutations can affect both local residue environments and the structural organization of protein complexes. Existing approaches often rely on handcrafted physicochemical, energetic, or evolutionary features, which introduce additional computational costs and require domain-specific knowledge. In this work, we propose MPFIL, a multi-level protein feature integration framework for predicting mutation-induced protein-protein binding affin ity changes. MPFIL integrates structural and sequential infor mation to characterize mutation effects from complementary perspectives. Its structural feature extraction module captures mutation-induced structural changes and differential information between wild-type and mutant complexes, while sequence feature extraction modules model local residue context and long-range dependencies. The resulting features are integrated for {triangleup}{triangleup}G prediction. We evaluate MPFIL on three benchmark datasets. Experimental results demonstrate competitive and consistent performance across different protein complex settings, while ablation studies verify the contribution of the structural and sequential features. These results support the effectiveness of multi-level protein feature integration for modeling mutation induced changes in protein-protein binding affinity.

items.title_en: NMR-measured Per-residue Electrostatic Potentials Reveal the Importance of Arginine-Lysine Balance on the Conformational Ensemble of Disordered Histone H3 Tails in Nucleosome Core Particles
items.title_zh: NMR测量的逐残基静电势揭示精氨酸-赖氨酸平衡对核小体核心颗粒中无序组蛋白H3尾部构象系综的重要性
items.abstract_en: Biophysical studies of chromatin have provided key insights into how the genome is regulated. Many atomic resolution structures of the fundamental building block of chromatin, the nucleosome core particle (NCP), as well as larger NCP arrays, both in isolation and in complex with effectors, or with post-translational modifications, have been elucidated. These provide in-depth pictures of key functional interactions. Considerably less information is available on the intrinsically disordered nucleosome tails that are critically important for higher order interactions in chromatin, and for transcription, DNA repair, and phase separation, and that serve as hubs for post-translational modifications. Here we focus on the tail of one of the four histones, histone-3 (H3), and measure electrostatic potentials at each of its amide proton positions in isolated NCPs via solution NMR spectroscopy. Using these potentials, in concert with molecular dynamics simulations, an ensemble of structures is calculated for WT H3 tails, as well as variants where all tail arginines are replaced by lysines (R2K) or vice versa (K2R). Our ensembles reveal that K2R tails have a higher propensity to occupy the most negatively charged region of the NCP between the DNA gyres than R2K or WT tails, while lysine enriched tails have an increased relative preference for the less negative regions near the DNA entry and exit points. The structural ensembles provide insight into differences in interactions between neighboring particles that lead to changes in diffusion and phase separation propensities between the NCP variants.

items.title_en: Cancer cells acquire cysteine directly from a reduced tumor microenvironment
items.title_zh: 癌细胞直接从还原性肿瘤微环境中获取半胱氨酸
items.abstract_en: The metabolic environment of a tumor is shaped by the nutrients available in its interstitial fluid, yet the redox composition of that fluid is poorly defined. Measuring sulfur metabolites in the interstitial fluid of tumors, matched healthy organs, and serum across three mouse models of cancer, we find that the tumor microenvironment (TME) is a chemically reduced compartment in which free cysteine predominates over its oxidized form, cystine. This is especially pronounced in the lung TME, where cystine is nearly absent. We further show that lung cancer cells take up cysteine and cystine with comparable efficiency and proliferate on cysteine alone, and that the abundant glutathione in the TME helps keep cysteine reduced through disulfide exchange. In a medium formulated to match the sulfur composition of the lung tumor interstitial fluid, cells become independent of cystine import through xCT. Cells cultured in this medium were resistant to glutaminase inhibitors, oxidants and ferroptosis inducers, and better maintained NADPH levels under oxidative challenge. These findings suggest that standard culture conditions overestimate the dependence of cancer cells on cystine uptake and their vulnerability to oxidative stress-targeting therapies.

items.title_en: Fine-tuning an intracellular allosteric pocket programs GPCR signaling bias
items.title_zh: 精细调控细胞内变构口袋可编程GPCR信号偏倚
items.abstract_en: Biased signaling of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers a route for precise therapeutics with fewer adverse effects. Intracellular allosteric ligands can impose such bias, yet how subtle chemical changes within these pockets reshape receptor-transducer coupling and downstream signaling remains unclear. Here, we systematically fine-tuned the intracellular allosteric pocket of neurotensin receptor 1 (NTSR1) through chemical modification of the {beta}-arrestin-biased ligand SBI-553. Minor changes to the ligand scaffold altered transducer-coupling preferences, generating distinct profiles of G-protein and {beta}-arrestin signaling. Cryo-electron microscopy structures of NTSR1-{beta}-arrestin2 complexes bound to designed allosteric probes revealed ligand-dependent remodeling of the intracellular cavity that reshapes the receptor-effector interface. Alanine scanning identified transducer-sensitive residues within and beyond the immediate ligand-contact region. In mice, SBI-553 and N065 produced distinct physiological profiles, with N065 improving survival in a lethal endotoxemia model. Finally, phosphoproteomic profiling revealed partially overlapping but distinct downstream signaling profiles among the three modulators. Together, these findings establish the intracellular allosteric pocket as a tunable determinant of transducer coupling and show that closely related modulators can generate distinct signaling and physiological profiles.

items.title_en: Modulation of planarian seizure-like activity via antiseizure medications
items.title_zh: 通过抗癫痫药物调节涡虫的癫痫样活动
items.abstract_en: Acute chemical exposure to organophosphorus compounds (OPs) arising from terrorist attacks or accidental poisonings pose a serious threat to human health. Acetylcholinesterase inhibition due to acute OP exposure causes a cholinergic crisis, manifested as increased secretions, respiratory distress, loss of consciousness, seizures, and ultimately death if left untreated. Benzodiazepines, such as midazolam, are currently used to stop OP-induced seizures, but must be administered within minutes after exposure to be effective. This makes midazolam impractical for large-scale civilian emergencies. Thus, there is a need to identify novel antiseizure medications (ASMs) that are equally effective even when administered later. It has been challenging to identify such compounds with traditional mammalian testing; high throughput screening assays that can quickly and cost-effectively evaluate many candidates for their potential as an ASM are needed. Planarians are aquatic invertebrates that are suitable organismal models for OP neurotoxicity studies due to the conservation of OP targets and their ability to metabolize OPs. Here, we built on our prior work that introduced a computational image analysis pipeline to quantify planarian seizure-like activity (pSLA) in two planarian species (Dugesia japonica and Girardia dorotocephala). We previously used this approach to characterize pSLA following acute exposure (up to 30 minutes) to seizurogenic compounds. In the present study, we asked whether pSLA induced by the OP pesticide parathion, pentylenetetrazole, or NMDA could be rescued by co-exposure to four ASMs: midazolam, topiramate, MK-801, and carbamazepine. All tested ASMs were effective at reducing parathion-induced pSLA in one planarian species. However, ASM responses varied substantially across proconvulsants and planarian species. Defining the molecular mechanisms underlying pSLA will be essential for establishing planarians as a reliable model for ASM discovery.

items.title_en: A pump-leak model of epithelia reveals the roles of paracellular pathways in water transport & the importance of boundary conditions
items.abstract_en: We develop a pump-leak model of epithelial transport, where the flux of water through the epithelium is modeled as a compartment, or sink, whose volume grows linearly with time. A method is described for calculating the voltage in the sink compartment, as well as analytical solutions to the system of equations. We show how growing boundary conditions can be used to model a scenario where water and ion fluxes are possible in the steady state. It is possible to drive a continuous flux of water through an epithelium that is powered by the Na+ pump establishing small osmotic gradients between compartments. We show that paracellular pathways play a crucial role in the operation of epithelial transport by ensuring that the flux through the epithelium is electroneutral. For the Na+ pump situated on the basolateral membrane, water fluxes can be directed in the same direction as the Na+ ion by having a high Na+ conductance on the apical membrane and high K+ conductance on the basolateral membrane. Flipping these conductances changes the direction of water fluxes. We introduce a graphic formalism that makes clear the precise mechanism of water transfer, showing the osmotic and electrical constraints. We demonstrate that it is possible when the extracellular osmolarity is low (~10mOsm) for the intracellular osmolarity to exceed that of the former considerably and produce a hyperosmolar solution.

items.title_en: Human prion proteins and mutants through the lens of systems biology
items.abstract_en: Autocatalytic conformational changes of cellular prion proteins (PrPC) to the {beta}-sheet-enriched scrapie isoform (PrPSC) drive prion diseases, yet the precise molecular mechanisms remain unclear. To address this, we employ a multi-pronged framework integrating network-theoretic analyses, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and experimental validation to characterize critical residues governing human PrP (huPrP) structural integrity. Residue Interaction Networks (RINs) of: (A) wild-type (WT) huPrP, and, (B) five disease-associated point mutants (Met166Val, Glu220Lys, Glu200Lys, Asp178Asn, and Ser170Asn) were evaluated using three rigorous network methods: centrality measures, Shortest Path Alteration Fraction (SPAF), and Differential Networks (DN). Across all the diverse point mutations, five residues (Met206, Val209, Val210, Met213, and Cys214) consistently exhibit high centrality scores. SPAF and DN analyses demonstrate that alterations at these positions disrupt connectivity and increase the propensity for misfolding and protease resistance. To validate these topological findings, key residues within the C-terminal domain (121-230) were substituted via site-directed mutagenesis. Thermal denaturation monitored by circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy reveals that the Met213Ala substitution significantly lowers the melting temperature, Tm, relative to the WT, whereas the Val210Ala variant unfolds with a Tm comparable to the WT. Furthermore, MD simulations of de novo AlphaFold-predicted mutant structures corroborate these findings. Mutants exhibit greater structural flexibility and deviation, with average root Mean Square Deviations rising from 0.18 nm (WT) to 0.32 nm (Cys214Ala), 0.29 nm (Met206Ala), and 0.25 nm (Val210Lys). This integration of theoretical and experimental techniques provides a robust framework for identifying critical determinants of protein stability.

items.title_en: Wasting is essential: cachexia is driven by a wound-healing adaptation
items.abstract_en: Background: Several explanations have been given for why cachexia occurs in the presence of severe acute wounds and chronic diseases. None of these explanations address the scope of clinical settings in which cachexia has been observed, nor do they account for the failure of nutritional support to reverse cachexia. We hypothesize that induced muscle wasting (IMW) is an adaptation to support wound healing, and when a wound does not heal, prolonged IMW leads to cachexia. Methods: To evaluate this hypothesis, we developed a mathematical model of IMW. In this model, we compared the time needed for wound healing when IMW was present and when it was inhibited. We also measured the relationship between the pathogen growth rate and final patient muscle mass for chronic diseases such as cancer and tuberculosis, demonstrating the onset of cachexia. Finally, we simulated the effects of nutritional support and contrasted the outcomes of when IMW was present and when it was inhibited. Results: Acute wound healing was ~2-6 times longer without IMW than with IMW. For chronic wounds, steady-state muscle mass strongly depended on the growth rate of the pathogenic agent. Inhibiting IMW was more effective at preventing acute muscle mass loss than nutritional support, and the benefit of nutritional support was enhanced by inhibiting IMW. Nutritional support also increased the speed of healing acute wounds when IMW was inhibited. For cancer with high growth rate, giving nutritional support alone had a negligible effect on steady-state muscle mass. But when IMW was inhibited, muscle mass loss was attenuated. With IMW inhibition, nutritional support with the normal diet was able to abrogate muscle mass loss entirely. Conclusions: Inhibiting IMW slows the healing of acute wounds, supporting our hypothesis that IMW is an adaptation to support rapid wound healing. Our experiments demonstrate that nutritional support is insufficient to prevent severe muscle mass loss while IMW continues. But when IMW is inhibited, nutritional support restores normal levels of muscle mass for both acute and chronic wounds, as well as increasing the rate of wound healing. Discovering and developing methods to inhibit IMW for clinical use will be essential to restore patient muscle mass, ease suffering, and reduce mortality.

items.title_en: Gene-gene and Gene-Environment Interactions Improve Genetic Risk Predictions for Complex Diseases
items.abstract_en: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) assume additive SNP effects, yet genetic risk also arises from interactions between loci and environmental factors that contribute to broad-sense heritability. We developed an extended PRS (ePRS) framework for type 2 diabetes (T2D) that incorporates locus-by-locus non-additive effects beyond those captured by additive single-locus PRS or linkage disequilibrium (LD) tagging. These were modelled as interaction-informed cumulative burden (G+G; summed allele counts), epistasis-screened (GxG; allele count products), and gene-environment effects derived from cardiometabolic variables in electronic health records. Across 235,000 UK Biobank participants, five complementary ePRS models captured largely non-overlapping high-risk individuals, suggesting that a key to individual risk predictions comprises the inclusion of multiple interaction-driven biological components rather than a single signal. A composite score was predictive over traditional additive PRS and predictive of T2D among individuals whose clinical symptoms fall within normal ranges.

items.title_en: A Unified Flexible Large Polysomnography Model for Sleep Staging and Downstream Clinical Screening
items.abstract_en: Polysomnography (PSG) is central to sleep medicine, yet its analysis remains hindered by labor-intensive manual scoring and limited cross-center generalizability. We present LPSGM, a large-scale PSG model trained on 220,500 hours of data from 16 public datasets (24,000 recordings) that addresses two challenges: cross-center sleep staging generalization and PSG-based screening of narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), and depression. LPSGM integrates domain-adaptive pre-training, flexible channel configurations, and a unified architecture to accommodate heterogeneous recording protocols. In prospective validation, LPSGM achieves expert-level sleep staging ({kappa} = 0.845 {+/-} 0.066 vs. inter-expert {kappa} = 0.850 {+/-} 0.102) and matches fully supervised models on independent private cohorts. For downstream screening, LPSGM achieves 84.2% accuracy ({kappa} = 0.761) in three-class narcolepsy classification, with cross-institutional transfer for normal-versus-abnormal hypersomnia yielding an AUC of 0.879. Severe OSA screening reaches an AUC of 0.874 without access to respiratory signals. Depression symptom screening achieves an AUC of 0.801 in a surrogate-labeled APPLES cohort, and cross-dataset transfer to an independent clinically diagnosed cohort reaches an AUC of 0.965. These results suggest that LPSGM's pre-trained representations capture sleep-related signatures that generalize across institutions and support PSG-based screening of clinically relevant conditions. The code and pre-trained model are publicly available at https://github.com/Deng-GuiFeng/LPSGM.

items.title_en: Familial factors inflate the estimated effects of genetic liability to ADHD on behavioural outcomes
items.abstract_en: Background: People with ADHD have worse health, behavioural and social outcomes, widely interpreted as evidence that ADHD causes these harms, justifying early identification and treatment. But ADHD clusters in families, and conventional studies cannot separate the effect of a person's own ADHD from the family environment in which it arises. We used a family-based genetic design to distinguish the two. Methods: We used up to 22 genome-wide significant variants associated with ADHD (38,691 cases, 186,843 controls) to estimate effects of genetic liability to ADHD on 16 health and behavioural outcomes. We compared population-based estimates with family-based estimates from within-sibship analyses of up to 164,220 siblings. We tested for heterogeneity between the designs, and applied sensitivity analyses. We involved individuals with lived experience of ADHD in interpreting the findings and shaping how the clinical/public-health implications were described. Findings: Population-based analyses implied that greater genetic liability to ADHD increased smoking, alcohol use and depressive symptoms, and reduced educational attainment, age at first child and cognitive performance. In family-based analyses, these effects attenuated. For example, the effect on number of depressive symptoms fell from 0.059 SD (95% CI 0.039, 0.080) to 0.002 SD (-0.052, 0.055), and age at first child increased from -0.045 SD (-0.058, -0.033) to 0.003 SD (-0.040, 0.047), with significant differences between designs (p=0.048 and p=0.034). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. Interpretation: Much of the excess health and behavioural burden attributed to ADHD may reflect the family and environmental context in which ADHD occurs, rather than an individual's own ADHD. Interventions targeting the individual might not reduce these outcomes as much as expected. Distinguishing such effects requires family-based designs. Funding: Medical Research Council, UK Research and Innovation, Research Council of Norway, US National Institute of Mental Health, and Australian National Health and Medical Research Council.

items.title_en: Clinical Significance and Distribution of Cerebrospinal Fluid Type IV Oligoclonal Band Pattern in Neurological Disorders: A Retrospective Analysis
items.abstract_en: Background and Objectives: To characterize the clinical features and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings of patients exhibiting a type IV oligoclonal band (OCB) pattern, defined by the presence of identical IgG bands in both CSF and serum. Methods: This retrospective observational study included all consecutive adult patients with a type IV pattern detected during routine CSF analysis at Geneva University Hospitals in 2023. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were collected through chart review. Results: A total of 178 patients were included. The mean age was 60.2 years (SD 16.5), and 51.7% were female. The type IV pattern was most frequently observed in non-inflammatory neurological diseases (NIND) (n=103, 57.9%). Other inflammatory neurological diseases accounted for 37 cases (20.7%), multiple sclerosis was identified in 8 patients (4.5%), and peripheral nervous system disorders were present in 20 patients (11.2%). Systemic inflammatory comorbidities were observed in 40 patients (22.5%). An elevated albumin quotient was present in 73 patients (41%) and was most common among those with CNS infections, aseptic meningitis, CNS neoplastic diseases, and peripheral nervous system disorder. Repeated CSF analyses demonstrated temporal fluctuations in the type IV pattern in some patients, without corresponding changes in diagnosis. Discussion: The type IV pattern is predominantly associated with NIND and is relatively uncommon in multiple sclerosis. Although it may reflect systemic immune activation and/or blood brain barrier dysfunction in certain inflammatory conditions, its clinical significance remains nonspecific. These findings support cautious interpretation of the type IV pattern in routine clinical practice.

items.title_en: Educational expectations and needs of individuals scheduled for breast surgery within the Primary Nursing Model: a qualitative study
items.abstract_en: Background. A diagnosis of breast cancer may represent a potentially destabilizing event, with significant physical, psychological, and social implications. Individuals scheduled for breast surgery require clear, understandable, and personalized information to prepare for surgery and manage the postoperative period. However, a discrepancy may arise between perceived informational needs and the information actually received. The Primary Nursing model, based on continuity of care and the presence of a designated primary nurse, may promote greater personalization of nurse-led patient education. Aim. To explore the experiences of individuals scheduled for breast surgery in relation to the nurse-led patient education received throughout the perioperative pathway, in order to understand their educational expectations, informational needs, and perceptions of the usefulness of the educational interventions provided within the Primary Nursing model. Design. A qualitative study with a phenomenological orientation. Methods. The study will be conducted at the European Institute of Oncology. Participants will be recruited through convenience sampling among individuals diagnosed with breast cancer who have undergone surgery and received the nurse-led discharge education routinely provided. Approximately 20 participants are expected to be enrolled; the final sample size will be determined according to the principle of data saturation. Data will be collected through semi-structured interviews conducted approximately two weeks after discharge by a member of the research team who is not involved in the participants Clinical care. The interviews, lasting approximately 30-40 minutes, will be audio-recorded with prior consent, transcribed verbatim, and assigned a sequential identification code. Sociodemographic data and clinical information extracted from the medical records will also be collected. The transcripts will be analyzed using thematic analysis according to Braun and Clarke, with a phenomenological orientation. Expected contribution. The study may contribute to understanding potential discrepancies between educational expectations, informational needs, and the perceived usefulness of the information received, thereby informing clinical practice toward personalized educational interventions consistent with continuity of care.

items.title_en: Statistical Analysis Plan for the REDEP study: Effectiveness of dual-mobility cups for preventing dislocation after primary total hip arthroplasty by a posterolateral approach compared to unipolar cups in elderly patients
items.abstract_en: Periprosthetic hip dislocation is a frequent complication after primary total hip arthroplasty. Observational studies suggest that dual mobility cups may reduce dislocation risk to approximately 1%, but definitive randomized evidence supporting their routine use in primary total hip arthroplasty is absent. The REDEP trial is the first prospective, randomized controlled trial that compares dual mobility cups with unipolar cups in patients [≥]70 years who electively undergo primary total hip arthroplasty via a posterolateral approach. The primary objective of the trial is to determine the difference in the number of patients who suffer a periprosthetic dislocation of the hip within 1 year after primary total hip arthroplasty in this population. Other outcomes include the difference in the total number of hip dislocations (including recurrent dislocations within patients), differences in patient-reported outcome measures, and differences in the incidence of (serious) adverse events. This statistical analysis plan describes the primary statistical analysis for the REDEP study. The analyses described herein were defined prior to database lock and unblinding. Secondary analyses will be described in subsequent versions of this statistical analysis plan.

items.title_en: Implementation of high-dose glucocorticoids and opioid consumption in the first 24 hours after elective hip and knee arthroplasty: a natural experiment study of 47,317 procedures in Eastern Denmark
items.abstract_en: Background: In Denmark, high-dose perioperative glucocorticoids were implemented stepwise for patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA), total knee arthroplasty (TKA), and unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA). We aimed to estimate the opioid-sparing effect of adding a single high dose of glucocorticoids to the analgesic regimen. Methods: In this prespecified analysis of a multicentre natural experiment using electronic health record data, we included all elective THA, TKA, or UKA procedures performed in Eastern Denmark from 2017-2025, with no exclusion criteria. At each centre, procedures before implementation of high-dose glucocorticoids served as controls, whereas procedures after implementation comprised the intervention group. A high dose was defined as [≥]16 mg or 0.2 mg/kg dexamethasone or [≥]80 mg methylprednisolone. The primary outcome was the adjusted between-group difference in 0-24h opioid consumption. The minimal important difference was 5 mg IV morphine equivalents. Secondary outcomes were maximum 0-10 numerical rating scale (NRS) pain score, incidence of opioid-related adverse events, hospital length of stay, and days alive and out of hospital at 30 days. Results: We analysed 47,317 procedures performed at nine centres: 13,010 controls and 34,307 in the intervention group. During the study period, five of nine centres implemented high-dose glucocorticoids for THA patients, two of eight for TKA/UKA patients. High-dose glucocorticoids were administered to 6% and 92% of patients before and after implementation, respectively. The implementation was associated with an adjusted mean reduction of 3.8 mg IV morphine equivalents (95% CI 3.3 to 4.3) and a 0.8-point lower maximum recorded pain score (99% CI 0.7 to 0.9) in the first 24 hours, with no statistically significant differences in the remaining outcomes. Conclusions: Implementation of high-dose glucocorticoids was associated with only a small drop in opioid consumption, below the minimal important difference. Online registration: https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.11.11.25339982

items.title_en: CREBBP variants underlying Menke-Hennekam syndrome exhibit histone acetyltransferase hyperactivity with divergent phase behaviors
items.abstract_en: Menke-Hennekam syndrome (MKHK) is a neurodevelopmental disease characterized by specific pathogenic regions within the transcriptional coactivator CREB-binding protein (CREBBP). CREBBP regulates gene expression through histone acetyltransferase (HAT) activity and involves IDR-dependent transcriptional condensates. Although domain-specific phenotypes and distinct DNA methylation episignatures have been recognized in MKHK, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain widely unclear. In this study, we identified a recurrent missense variant, p.(R1868W) [R1868W]) and a novel splice variant r.5963_5969del,p.(Cys1723Thrfs*19) [C1723fs] in two families clinically diagnosed with MKHK and manifesting developmental delay, characteristic facial features, and growth impairment. R1868W and C1723fs exhibited increased auto-, nonhistone protein, and histone acetylation. Despite these shared enzymatic abnormalities, the variants promoted divergent disruption in liquid-liquid phase separation. The recurrent CBP-ID4 variant R1868W activated the formation of low-mobility aberrant nuclear condensates, whereas the C-terminal, truncating variant C1723fs, impaired condensate formation and showed diffuse nuclear localization. Treatment with the selective p300/CBP HAT inhibitor A485 partially restored condensate dynamics and fusion-relaxation behavior in R1868W. Furthermore, R1868W recruited BRD4 around condensates in an acetylation-dependent manner, which was suppressed by the BET inhibitor JQ1. Together, these findings suggest that aberrant condensate material properties arising from disrupted CREBBP IDR-dependent regulation play a critical role in the molecular pathogenesis of MKHK.

items.title_en: Comparing the Phenotypic and Genetic Differences Between Autistic Regression and Autism Without Regression Using the SPARK Cohort
items.abstract_en: The biology of autistic regression (Autreg) remains poorly understood. We investigated Autreg's phenotypic and genetic landscape in 51 633 individuals from the SPARK cohort. We calculated the frequencies of parental-reported language regression and regression affecting social, play, toileting, and/or other developmental domains, and ages at skill regression and regain within SPARK. We compared developmental milestones, quantitative developmental measures, and selected other phenotypes in Autreg and autism without regression (Autnreg). Rare damaging coding variants and polygenic scores (PGS) in Autreg and Autnreg were compared using genome sequencing data. Rare variants were analyzed using the Transmission And De novo Association (TADA) framework in 1 107 Autreg and 974 Autnreg individuals, followed by pathway enrichment analysis. PGS for autism, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, epilepsy, and schizophrenia were initially compared. PGS validation was conducted in 14 001 Autnreg and 11 638 Autreg individuals using larger SPARK genotyping data. We identified regression in 43% of autistic individuals. Other regression occurred later than language regression, and 60% of skill regain occurred within two years. Autreg was associated with lower Vineland-3 Adaptive Behavior Composite scores (p twofold increased odds of epilepsy and intellectual disability (p<0.001). Developmental milestones and quantitative measures had modest differences. TADA analysis highlighted genes involved in nucleotide catabolism, transcription, and focal adhesion, with PTEN emerging as a strong candidate for Autreg. Schizophrenia PGS explained 0.087% of variance in liability to regression among autistic individuals. In conclusion, Autreg was associated with increased neurodevelopmental morbidity. Schizophrenia PGS and rare variants explained a minimal fraction of its etiology.

items.title_en: Cross-Sectional Study of Periodontal Oral Dental Foci of Infection (PODFI) in Medically Compromised Patients at Lille University Hospital
items.abstract_en: Oral dental foci of infection (ODFI), particularly those of periodontal origin, can trigger systemic inflammatory responses that may cause bacteraemia for medically compromised patients. Although guidelines recommend detection and elimination of these foci, precise data on the distribution of periodontal oral dental foci of infection (PODFI) risk within these populations remain scarce. This study aimed to describe periodontal sources of infection in medically compromised patients using a periodontal examination and follow-up form and a recently developed PODFI risk levels classification. This observational, retrospective, cross-sectional, single-center study evaluated medically compromised patients with periodontitis in the dental surgery department of the Lille University Hospital between September 2024 and September 2025. Periodontitis was diagnosed according to the 2017 Classification of Periodontal Diseases established at the 2017 World Workshop. The primary outcome was the distribution of PODFI risk levels (moderate, high, very high). Secondary outcomes aimed to describe periodontal conditions in a specific population of medically compromised patients. Thirty-nine patients were included in this study. Evaluation of PODFI risk (n = 34) revealed a predominance of moderate-risk profiles (67.6 %) and a significant proportion of high-risk profiles (32.4 %); no low-risk or very high-risk profiles were observed. Generalized periodontal inflammation was very common (92 %), with a median of 26 bleeding on probing (BOP) sites and 71 plaque-positive sites, showing a positive correlation (R = 0.52, p = 0.002). Severe and active forms of periodontitis predominated (n = 39), with 74.4 % of cases classified as stage III (28.2 %) or stage IV (46.2 %), and grade B was the most common (56.4 %), followed by grade C (38.5 %) (p = 0.025). Medically compromised patients have a high prevalence of severe and active periodontitis, with nearly one-third of them classified as being at high risk for infection. The recently developed periodontal oral dental foci of infection (PODFI) classification provides a structured and clinically relevant tool for stratifying infection risk and guiding treatment decisions. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm the validity of these PODFI risk levels.
