items.title_en: Between- and Within-Person Coupling of Nocturnal Heart Rate and Glucose: Retrospective, Real-World Observational Study of 105,196 Nights From 2648 Adults Using Ultrahuman Ring and Continuous Glucose Monitoring
items.abstract_en: Background: Higher resting or sleeping heart rate (HR) has been associated with poorer glucose metabolism in adults without diabetes. However, these associations were estimated across individuals, and within-person characterization of this co-regulation during naturalistic sleep in large free-living cohorts remains limited. Objective: This study aimed to determine whether average sleeping HR, an indirect index of cardiac autonomic tone, is associated with nocturnal glucose within a participant and between participants, and whether night-to-night irregularity in sleep duration, sleep onset, and wake time is associated with nocturnal glycemia. Methods: In this retrospective observational study, adults who concurrently wore an Ultrahuman Ring and a continuous glucose monitor between January 2024 and June 2025 were analyzed. After participant- and night-level filtering, the cohort comprised 2648 participants from 87 countries, contributing 105,196 paired nights. Each predictor was decomposed into within- and between-participant components by person-mean centering and entered a single linear mixed-effects model with a random intercept for participant, adjusted for age, body mass index (BMI), and sex. Outcomes were nocturnal mean glucose, nocturnal glucose coefficient of variation (CV), and nocturnal time in range (70-110 mg/dL). Per-participant slopes were fitted in participants with sustained wear (at least 30 nights spanning at least 60 days). Estimates were re-derived under trimming and robust-regression specifications and refitted within BMI and regional strata. Results: Higher average sleeping HR was associated with higher nocturnal mean glucose both within participants (+5.7 mg/dL per 10 bpm, 95% CI 5.4-5.9) and between participants (+6.5 mg/dL, 95% CI 5.6-7.3; both P<.001). Within participants, higher sleeping HR was also associated with higher glucose CV (+1.37 percentage points, 95% CI 1.30-1.43) and lower time in range (-6.3 percentage points, 95% CI -6.7 to -6.0). Of the 911 sustained-wear participants, 701 (76.9%, 95% CI 74.1%-79.6%) had a positive individual slope (median of +5.2 mg/dL per 10 bpm). The association survived in every BMI stratum and in all 5 regional strata. Sleep-duration irregularity was associated with mean glucose between participants (+4.1 mg/dL per 30 minutes, 95% CI 2.6-5.7) but only weakly within them (+0.23 mg/dL). Within participants, a night 1 standard deviation above a participants own mean sleeping HR corresponded to 2.5 mg/dL higher nocturnal mean glucose. Conclusions: Average sleeping HR was associated with glucose within individuals as well as between them, indicating that the relationship is not attributable solely to stable between-person differences and reflects, at least in part, night-to-night covariation. The association was modest, but discernible in naturalistic sleep across geographies. Sleep-duration irregularity was associated with nocturnal glycemia mainly between individuals.

items.title_en: From non-uptake during early adolescence to acceptance during a catch-up campaign: a qualitative study of changing HPV vaccination decisions across two life stages among young women in Amsterdam, the Netherlands
items.abstract_en: Background: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination effectively prevents HPV-related disease, but its population-level impact depends on sufficient coverage. In 2023-2024, the Netherlands offered free HPV vaccination to individuals aged 19-27 years through a national catch-up campaign. For women, this was a second opportunity, as they had been offered vaccination at ages 9-13 through the National Immunisation Programme (NIP). Back then, uptake was relatively low (46-57% in these birth cohorts), but uptake increased to 55-63% following the catch-up vaccination. This campaign provided an apt opportunity to explore the factors underlying previous and current HPV vaccination decisions among the same women across two life stages. Methods: Between May 2023 and May 2024, 16 semi-structured interviews were conducted in Amsterdam with women who accepted HPV vaccination during the catch-up after non-uptake during early adolescence. Interviews explored factors influencing non-uptake and later acceptance, guided by the Health Belief Model and additional sociocultural constructs. Data were analysed using thematic analysis with open and theory-guided coding in MAXQDA. Results: Non-uptake during early adolescence was primarily shaped by parental decision-making, cultural and religious norms, fear of side effects, low perceived susceptibility to HPV and limited self-efficacy. Acceptance in young adulthood was driven by greater autonomy, higher perceived susceptibility, increased trust in accumulated vaccine evidence and accessible vaccination infrastructure. Peer influence replaced parental influence as the dominant social factor. Conclusion: HPV vaccine decision-making is a dynamic process rather than fixed. Permanent catch-up HPV vaccination opportunities would enable young adults to make autonomous vaccination decisions as their circumstances change.

items.title_en: Stage-dependent associations of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome with Cognitive Decline, Depression, and Neuroimaging Signatures in multi-regional older adults
items.abstract_en: Background Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a multisystem condition associated with adverse outcomes, yet its impact on age-related cognitive health remains understudied. We examined associations of CKM with neurocognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes, modifiable physical and psychosocial factors contributing to cognitive impairment across CKM stages, and neuroimaging correlates. Methods Global aging cohorts (mean follow-up 6.5 years) and the Cohort Studies of Memory in an International Consortium (5.4 years) were used. CKM stages (0-4) were defined according to AHA framework. Longitudinal domain-specific cognitive changes were assessed using linear mixed-effects models, and depressive symptoms using generalized linear regression with individual participant data approach. Population-attributable fractions were estimated for six modifiable factors associated with cognitive impairment across CKM stages. Cross-sectional associations with 34 neuroimaging biomarkers were examined in UK Biobank. Results Among 28,242 participants, advanced CKM stages (3-4) were associated with accelerated cognitive decline, particularly in attention, executive function, and language. Associations were stronger in younger individuals, men, and those with less education, but not modified by APOE 4 status. Advanced CKM stages were associated with depressive symptoms among cognitively unimpaired individuals. Modifiable factors accounted for 24.8% of cognitive impairment risk across CKM stages, mainly social isolation (7.0%), depressive symptoms (5.2%), and physical inactivity (5.2%). Advanced CKM stages were linked to widespread MRI alterations (27 biomarkers), especially white matter hyperintensity. Conclusion Advanced CKM stages are associated with accelerated cognitive decline and greater cerebrovascular burden. Addressing psychosocial factors and physical inactivity, alongside management of CKM risk factors, may help reduce cognitive impairment.

items.title_en: COMMUNITY KNOWLEDGE AND ATTITUDE TOWARDS POLIO IMMUNIZATION IN NORTHERN NIGERIA
items.abstract_en: ckground: Poliomyelitis remains a public health concern where population immunity is incomplete and circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus (cVDPV) persists. Although Nigeria interrupted wild poliovirus transmission in 2020, cVDPV cases continue to pose challenges, particularly in parts of Northern Nigeria. Methods: This multicentre descriptive cross-sectional study evaluated community knowledge and attitudes towards polio immunization across 37 Local Government Areas (LGAs) in 20 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). A multistage sampling strategy was utilized to select 1,850 adult respondents (50 per LGA) spanning rural, semi-urban, and urban settlements. Results: Overall, 40.4% (n = 747) of respondents demonstrated good knowledge, while 58.4% (n = 1,080) displayed positive attitudes towards polio immunization. A striking disparity was observed across residence classifications: respondents in urban/semi-urban LGAs exhibited significantly higher levels of good knowledge (51.7%, 569/1,100) compared to those in rural LGAs (23.7%, 178/750; {chi} 2 = 144.00, df = 1, p < 0.001). Main sources of information were health workers (33.0%) and radio (21.1%). Conclusion: Knowledge deficits persist in rural Northern Nigerian communities despite favorable attitudes. Interventions must prioritize localized risk communication, traditional and religious leadership involvement, and primary healthcare integration.

items.title_en: On the stability of learning
items.abstract_en: Learning algorithms are usually analyzed under the assumption that informative gradients are continuously available. But this is not always true---learning signals in biological neural networks, for example, may be sparse, local, and only intermittently available at any given synapse. In this work, we show that if gradient information is noisy and only intermittently available, learning may be unstable. In particular, even if average learning dynamics converge to the correct optimum, variance in learning may be asymptotically infinite. We explore this point in a number of analytically tractable settings, including single-layer and multi-layer linear networks, and derive explicit conditions under which learning is stable. These conditions complement, but are conceptually distinct from, existing conditions related to the stability of stochastic gradient descent. Our work demonstrates that unbiased credit assignment is not enough for reliable learning; sufficiently frequent and informative feedback is also required, which yields an additional constraint on models of biologically plausible learning.

items.title_en: Dynamic heart rate variability for classification of arrhythmia burden
items.abstract_en: Purpose: Heart rate variability (HRV) may provide information beyond heart rate (HR) for identifying arrhythmia burden, but the value of temporal HRV variation remains unclear. This study developed a dynamic HRV measure quantifying the interquartile range of window-level root mean square of successive RR-interval differences (IQRRMSSD) and evaluated its utility in classifying total abnormal-beat and premature ventricular contraction (PVC) burden compared with the conventional RR-based HRV measure, RMSSD. Methods: Manually annotated 30-minute ECG recordings from 43 individuals were analyzed using overlapping windows. A linear support vector classifier was used to classify individuals as having high or low arrhythmia burden, defined using 1% and 10% burden thresholds. Four feature sets were evaluated: HR alone, HR with RMSSD, HR with IQRRMSSD, and all three measures. Performance was assessed using repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation. Results: HRV-containing feature sets generally outperformed HR alone, depending on outcome and threshold. At the 1% threshold, IQRRMSSD showed particularly high sensitivity for total abnormal-beat and PVC burden ($0.970 \pm 0.064$ and $0.882 \pm 0.193$, respectively). At the 10% threshold, conventional RMSSD showed the strongest overall discrimination, achieving a ROC-AUC of 0.947 for PVC burden. Combined features sometimes improved the sensitivity-specificity balance but not overall discrimination. Conclusion: These findings suggest that a conventional RR-based HRV measure is informative for elevated ectopic burden, while a dynamic HRV measure may provide complementary information for lower-burden abnormalities.

items.title_en: A theory of noisy linear recurrent neural network learning dynamics
items.title_zh: 含噪线性循环神经网络学习动力学理论
items.abstract_en: Biological neural networks are noisy: their dynamics involve difficult-to-predict fluctuations which are likely due not just to chaos, but also to a variety of low-level biophysical processes. Despite the omnipresence of intrinsic noise, its theoretical consequences are incompletely understood, especially in the context of learning. For example, does noise meaningfully shape representation learning, or is it better viewed as a nuisance factor whose presence or absence changes little about what solution is found and when? Here, we argue that intrinsic noise can significantly modulate representation learning in recurrent neural networks (RNNs), since it can strongly break solution-space degeneracies and in some cases control whether a non-degenerate solution exists at all. We show that this is true for an analytically tractable model of noisy RNN learning with a linear activation function and white noise inputs. We find that, in the so-called rich regime (where weights are initialized with small values), noise strongly modulates the directions in which the read-in, readout, and recurrent weights align. Moreover, we find that noise produces a kind of phase transition: for sufficiently high noise, a non-degenerate solution is not even optimal if parameter scales are limited (e.g., via regularization). These results extend recent analytic work on RNN representation learning and show that noise can act as a fundamental determinant of representations.

items.title_en: Phase response approach to networked neural activity models with delays
items.abstract_en: Networks of delay-coupled neural mass models alternate between synchrony and anti-phase locking as the delay between brain regions increases. The origin of these delay-dependent bands has remained unclear. Here, we show that a single function, the phase interaction function $H$ of an isolated node, predicts where the bands occur and explains why they repeat. For a Wilson--Cowan model with intra-nodal delay $τ$ and inter-nodal delay $ρ$, we compute the limit cycle and phase response, and hence $H$, by harmonic balance. Each band boundary is a zero of $H'$ shifted by the phase lag $Ωρ$, so the bands repeat in $ρ$ with the oscillation period. Simulations of the full delay-differential networks confirm these predictions, from two nodes, where predicted frequencies agree to second order in the coupling strength, to rings, where the theory also identifies coexisting stable twisted states that random initial conditions rarely reach. At weak coupling, the delays at which synchrony gains or loses stability are set by the node dynamics alone, whereas stable anti-phase states require a bipartite network. For a macaque connectome, metastability peaks at the edges of the synchrony bands, where the stability margin of phase-locking vanishes. The reduction is accurate for coupling strengths well below the slowest Floquet exponent of the node, beyond which a phase--amplitude description is needed. More broadly, vanishing phase-locking stability provides a simple route to metastability in delay-coupled oscillator networks and a candidate mechanism for the flexible coordination of brain dynamics.

items.title_en: Multiscale MIGHT: Modeling Local and Systemic Particle Transport in the Cardiovascular System
items.abstract_en: Analytical models of signaling molecule (SM) transport in the cardiovascular system (CVS) force a choice between whole-body scope and vessel-level resolution: Pharmacokinetic models for systemic transport lump each organ and lack small-scale structure, whereas synthetic molecular communication (MC) channel models resolve branched vessel networks (VNs) only for a single pass or capture recirculation only in topologically simple loops, and only partially include SM degradation. To close this gap, we propose Multiscale MIGHT, an extension of the Mixture of Inverse Gaussians for Hemodynamic Transport (MIGHT) model that jointly captures branched topologies, closed-loop circulation, organ clearance, and chemical degradation of SMs. First, we connect the ends of a branched VN to form a closed loop with local and global SM degradation, model the closed-loop channel impulse response for arbitrary transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx) positions as a Laplace-domain feedback system, and approximate it in closed form by an inverse Gaussian mixture over multi-pass trajectories. The model is validated against finite-element simulations in COMSOL. Second, we set up a whole-body model, where an exemplary local VN, resolved at vessel-level detail, is embedded into the remaining systemic circulation, represented by lumped organ blocks. We simulate whole-body SM transport for various Tx sites and SM species. Our results show that, at an Rx in a local VN, only the initial pass produces a distinct peak in the SM concentration, significantly shaped by the local vasculature in case of small Tx-Rx distances; subsequent passes arrive strongly dispersed and are shaped almost entirely by organ clearance and chemical degradation rather than by the local VN topology.

items.title_en: Escaping cells dilute CRISPR screen responses unequally across cell types
items.abstract_en: Single-cell CRISPR screens run in many cell types are used to compare how cell types respond to perturbation, to train models that transfer effects between them and to score such models. These uses assume that cells carrying a guide RNA had their target knocked down. Yet cells grow for days before sequencing: when an essential gene is knocked down, knocked-down cells are depleted or stop dividing while cells that escaped knockdown keep growing, and the measured response, an average over all cells carrying the guide, is diluted. We define the escape fraction of a perturbation as the share of its measured cells whose target was not effectively knocked down, and estimate it from each cell's counts of the targeted gene with a two-group mixture that recovers known fractions in simulated mixtures. In most cell types the escape fraction rises with how essential the gene is, it is higher in a later screen of the same cells, and it reaches about half of the measured cells in human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). It predicts how much each response is diluted: the response size falls to (1 - e)^2 of that of the knocked-down cells. Because the escape fraction differs between cell types, it changes all three uses: hESCs respond like K562 cells unless knockdown depletes them, the coefficient a simple transfer model learns is lowered by the dilution of the cell type it predicts, and a benchmark scored on all cells rewards predictions shrunk towards no change, partly because that ground truth is itself diluted. Where cells stop dividing instead, the response also contains expression differences between cell-cycle stages. Response sizes should be compared on knocked-down cells or corrected for the escape fraction.

items.title_en: mdRNAcat: A Molecular Dynamics RNA Catalog of REST2 Conformational Ensembles
items.abstract_en: Learning molecular models of RNA requires simulation data that capture conformational variability and provide consistent physical training signals. Here, we introduce mdRNAcat, a curated dataset of all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 48 RNA systems selected to promote sequence diversity. Each system is simulated using replica-exchange with solute scaling (REST2), with 32 Hamiltonian states and production lengths of 200-300 ns per state. The dataset provides atomic coordinates, instantaneous forces, and forces reevaluated under the unscaled reference Hamiltonian, together with structural annotations and replica-exchange metadata. Coordinates and forces are available at 1 ps intervals for the reference state and 100 ps intervals across all states in a standardized HDF5 format. We characterize conformational sampling, exchange behavior, base pairing, and sugar-pucker distributions to document the properties of the simulated ensembles. mdRNAcat provides a reusable resource for developing and evaluating data-driven RNA models, including coarse-grained force fields.

items.title_en: Comparing Measurements of Pictorial Depth: Conditions for Placing Methods, Observers and Depiction Styles on One Scale
items.abstract_en: Two observers can agree about what lies in front in a picture yet report different amounts of apparent depth. People report pictorial depth by judging which of two points looks nearer, setting a probe to match a surface, adjusting relative sizes, or rating three-dimensionality. Two such methods can agree closely without sharing a unit. We ask when different methods, observers, depiction styles and viewing conditions can share one scale. Each set of scores, a measurement block, is a graph node. Two blocks are linked only if their shared observations pass six checks fixed in advance, among them outcome type, removal of declared offsets and position effects, proportionality and covariance. If the adjusted shared patterns are exactly proportional, a connected graph fixes every block's gain, its relative scale factor. The checks accept proportionality only within a set margin, so a link supports the gains without proving exact proportionality. One unit is still not one depth coordinate. Suppose each block scores shared stimuli with its own origin and positive unit. A matrix-rank test then decides when a common coordinate is identified: when only one overall origin and unit remain free. If each shared stimulus, an anchor, is scored by exactly two blocks, this needs two disjoint sets of anchors, each connecting every block, their compatibility assumed, not tested. They also suffice, except for anchor values satisfying exact polynomial relations (probability zero for anchor values drawn from any distribution with a density). We adapt network gain estimation from test linking, with a loop-consistency check. A reanalysis of published probe settings on 3-D renderings passes one of 171 candidate depiction-style links through all six checks, each judged by its own 95% bound, unadjusted for the 171 pairs. Links between tasks remain untested; they need shared stimuli and a joint uncertainty model.

items.title_en: Estimating the Direct Impact of Influenza Vaccination and Vaccine-Averted Illnesses Using an Extended Static Compartmental Model
items.abstract_en: A previously developed static compartment model informed influenza program decisions by estimating the direct impact of influenza vaccination. To improve the estimation of the burden averted by vaccination, we extended this model to consider multiple influenza seasons, allow natural and vaccine-induced immunity to wane over time allow influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) to differ by hospitalized versus non-hospitalized influenza-associated illness, and measure deaths averted. For model demonstration, we created a synthetic Northern Hemisphere-like and year-round influenza activity dataset spanning four seasons among older adults (>65 years) and assumed VE against symptomatic illness of 37% (17%-53%) and VE against hospitalization of 45% (28%-59%). Under Northern Hemisphere-like activity and an existing vaccination program with an average annual vaccine coverage of 33%, vaccination averted 15.1% (95% UI: 12.2%-16.3%) of influenza-associated illnesses across four seasons; the annual prevented fraction for hospitalized deaths ranged from 14.4% (95% UI: 11.7%-16.8%) to 18.5% (95% UI: 14.9%-21.5%). Under a hypothetical year-round vaccination program with an annual coverage of 20%, vaccination averted 4.9% (95% UI: 3.8%-5.4%) of influenza-associated illnesses across four seasons; the annual prevented fraction for hospitalized deaths ranged from 5.5% (95% UI: 4.3%-6.5%) and 5.8% (95% UI: 4.8%-6.6%). These model extensions allow estimation of vaccine-averted burden across multiple seasons and diverse vaccination program settings, providing information to support influenza vaccination decision-making.

items.title_en: Modelled mortality benefits of reducing fibrinolysis resistance in sepsis: integrating observational and ex vivo data
items.abstract_en: Background. Suppressed fibrinolysis (fibrinolysis resistance) is increasingly recognised as a driver of organ failure in sepsis, yet trials in sepsis-induced coagulopathy have largely targeted coagulation rather than fibrinolysis. This study combined an observational ICU cohort with nested analyses of plasma fibrinolysis proteins and ex vivo reversibility, modelling the potential mortality reduction from restoring fibrinolytic capacity to inform trial design. Methods. In 188 adults admitted to ICU with sepsis, repeated tissue plasminogen activator (tPA)-enhanced viscoelastometric testing quantified fibrinolysis resistance as the fibrin adjusted lysis time (TPA-LT/FIBA10) and as ordinal Grades 1-3 of worsening resistance. Adjusted logistic regression and time-varying Cox models related fibrinolysis resistance to death within 28 days of admission, with unmeasured confounding assessed by E-values. In nested sub-studies, plasma fibrinolysis proteins were measured and whole blood was tested ex vivo for reversal of resistance by supplemental tPA, plasminogen, or an inhibitory antibody to a2-antiplasmin (a2AP iAb). Ex vivo effects were modelled onto the observed fibrinolysis resistance-mortality relationship using a hypothetical intervention distribution framework. Results. Each e-fold (~2.72) increase in TPA-LT/FIBA10 was associated with a 2.2-fold (95% CI 1.5-3.3) increase in the odds of death in the fully adjusted logistic model and a 2.3-fold (1.6-3.2) increased hazard in the time-varying Cox model. Comparing the least (Grade 1) with the worst (Grade 3) resistance state, the odds ratio was 7.4 (2.4-23) and the hazard ratio 6.7 (3.0-15). Associations were robust to unmeasured confounding, with E-values of 3-13. Grade 3 resistance showed the highest PAI-1/tPA and a2AP/plasminogen ratios. Ex vivo supplementation with plasminogen or a2AP iAb reversed fibrinolysis resistance from Grade 3 to Grade 1. Modelling these effects yielded hypothetical absolute mortality reductions of 18-21% across Grades 2 and 3, and 32-36% in Grade 3. Conclusions. Fibrinolysis resistance measured at the bedside in sepsis reflects mechanistically reversible changes in fibrinolytic balance ex vivo. Modelling reversal by plasminogen supplementation or a2AP inhibition yielded hypothetical absolute mortality reductions of up to 32% in the most severe resistance state. These hypothesis-generating estimates identify candidate interventions and provide a rationale for a clinical trial.

items.title_en: Prevalence and determinants of problematic khat use in Ethiopia
items.abstract_en: **Background** Evidence on khat use prevalence is substantial in Ethiopia and elsewhere. However, problematic khat use remains largely understudied because the concept has not been clearly defined or consistently measured. This study estimated the prevalence and determinants of problematic khat use among Ethiopian adults. **Methods** This descriptive cross-sectional analysis used baseline data from a prospective khat cohort study conducted in Butajira and adjacent districts in Central Ethiopia Regional State. We included 504 khat users who had chewed khat within the previous five years. Problematic khat use was assessed using the locally developed and validated 17-item Problematic Khat Use Screening Tool (PKUST-17). A score of >17 indicated problematic use. Binary and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify associated factors. **Results** Among the 504 khat users, most were male (82.3%), married (85.0%), and rural residents (70.8%). The prevalence of problematic khat use was 19.6%. Daily or near-daily khat users had eightfold higher odds of problematic use than occasional users (AOR = 8.05, 95% CI: 3.75-17.24). Stressful life events were associated with 3.48-fold higher odds of problematic use (AOR = 3.48, 95% CI: 1.56-7.76), while depressive symptoms were associated with 3.70-fold higher odds (AOR = 3.70, 95% CI: 2.00-6.75). **Conclusion** Problematic khat use affects approximately one in five khat users in Ethiopia. It is strongly associated with frequent khat use, stressful life events, and depressive symptoms. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify causal pathways and evaluate culturally appropriate prevention and treatment interventions.

items.title_en: Understanding widening socio-economic inequities in cardiovascular disease mortality in the Netherlands: A mixed methods protocol
items.abstract_en: Background: In the Netherlands, there is a substantial social gradient in mortality: individuals with higher socio-economic status are more likely to live longer lives than those with lower socio-economic status. There is evidence that this social gradient has widened since the mid-twentieth century, although why this has occurred is poorly understood. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) provides a particularly useful case study for understanding the mechanisms underlying this widening gradient. While CVD was historically the leading cause of death in the Netherlands, improvements in prevention and treatment have decreased CVD mortality, even as socio-economic inequalities in CVD mortality have increased. In this project, I aim to identify and test the mechanisms driving widening socio-economic inequities in CVD mortality over the last 75 years. Methods and analysis: This project uses mixed-methods. First, in participatory workshops, key stakeholders, e.g. policymakers, healthcare professionals, patient representatives, and individuals with lived experience of poverty, will co-create a conceptual model outlining the explanations linking socio-economic status and CVD in the Netherlands. Second, the conceptual model will provide the structure for the microsimulation, with the former defining which mechanisms will be represented in the latter. The microsimulation will maintain a common model structure across time, although population characteristics and individual trajectories will change to reflect successive twenty-year periods from the 1950s until today. The microsimulation will be validated by comparing simulated outcomes with historical data. Counterfactual scenarios will then be used to estimate the relative contribution of different mechanisms to the widening of socio-economic inequalities in CVD mortality. Ethics and dissemination: This project has been approved by the Social Sciences Research Ethics Committee of Wageningen University (approval number 2026-203). Participants will provide informed consent prior to participation. The microsimulation code will be made openly available, and findings will be disseminated through open-access publications, conference presentations, and a public summary co-designed with stakeholders.

items.title_en: MAScINSIGHT: A Real-World Data Study to Deepen Knowledge and Management of McCune-Albright Syndrome - Study Protocol for an Observational Study within OHDSI
items.abstract_en: Introduction McCune-Albright syndrome (MAS) is a rare congenital disorder affecting endocrine, skeletal and dermatological systems. MAS is often coded as fibrous dysplasia (FD) in routine health data, which includes other conditions and does not allow precise identification. This coding gap complicates reliable epidemiological estimates and clinical characterization. The study MAScINSIGHT aims to address this by investigating MAS features within FD-coded cohorts. Methods and analysis MAScINSIGHT is a retrospective observational study using a federated network of data in the OMOP Common Data Model. Routine data from multiple sites will be analyzed within a federated setting to assess endocrine abnormalities and treatment patterns in patients with FD or MAS. Ethics and dissemination Analyses will be performed locally at the data partner, with only aggregate statistics made available and centrally analyzed. The study protocol was approved by the ethics committee (reference number: 2026-18760-retrospektiv). Findings will be disseminated through open-access publications and patient-oriented reports.

items.title_en: Maternal Autoantibody Combinations as Predictors of Autism Risk: Retrospective Discovery and External Validation in a Prospective Cohort at Increased Risk
items.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Maternal Autoantibody-Related Autism (MARA) is a recently defined subset of autism characterized by specific combinations of maternal autoantibodies which cross the placenta and bind neurodevelopmentally critical target proteins. A clinical multi-ELISA MARA assay was recently rigorously analytically validated. The primary objective of this study was to assess the potential performance of this MARA autoantibody assay for predicting autism risk in high-risk populations. Secondary objectives were to establish the significant MARA autoantibody combinations and verify clinical discrimination in an external cohort. Methods: Bio-banked plasma samples from mothers of 420 autism and 335 typically developing (TD) children were analyzed by ELISA for MARA autoantibodies in combination. Transcendent autoantibody pairwise combinations were identified in discovery where both autoantibodies in a combination exceeded the values of every control participant. Permutation testing was used to establish that the probability of observed results significantly exceeded chance. Performance was then validated in an independent cohort (mothers of 42 autistic and 90 TD children). Results: Transcendent antibody levels were discovered in 70 mothers (16.7% of autism cases; no typically developing participants) in the discovery cohort. Specificity and positive predictive values for autism were 100% by construct. An external cohort showed similar performance with 14 (33.3%) transcendents. Permutation testing of each cohort demonstrated probabilities of transcendent cases to be significantly higher than expected be chance. Conclusions: The data reported here provides evidence for a high-risk subset of mothers of children with autism identified by the MARA autoantibody assay which enables further clinical validation.

items.title_en: A lifecourse perspective on sociodemographic intersectional inequalities in physical and mental health outcomes
items.abstract_en: Persistent inequalities in health outcomes continue to be a stubborn feature of many developed Western societies. To effectively understand health inequalities researchers must address two key criticisms: an overt focus on singular dimensions of disadvantage and a continuing need for longitudinal studies. Lifecourse intersectionality offers a framework to address these critiques through situating more nuanced and multidimensional understandings of the development of inequalities over time. We conduct a longitudinal Multilevel Analysis of Individual Heterogeneity and Discriminatory Accuracy (MAIHDA) examining both physical and mental health SF12 scores using UK Household Longitudinal Study data for adults (2009 to 2023). Forming intersections based on sex, ethnicity, generational cohort, education, and socioeconomic class, we identify a substantial degree of intersectional variation in our outcomes, and distinct differences in the development of intersectional inequalities in physical and mental health over the lifecourse. Intersectional inequalities are more pronounced for mental health compared to physical health, particularly at younger and older ages. In both cases, inequalities are additively patterned with generation and sex appearing most important to mental health and socioeconomic differences being stronger for physical health. However, our results also emphasise heterogeneity in the identified lifecourse intersectional effects, particularly in relation to how the patterning of the sociodemographic components for mental health vary by generational cohort. We therefore help reveal important complexity in the development of health inequalities in the UK and highlight the utility of longitudinal intersectional MAIHDA as a tool for quantitative intersectional researchers.

items.title_en: Motion-robust high-resolution 3D-GRASE pseudo-continuous ASL perfusion imaging at 3T
items.abstract_en: Purpose: High resolution arterial spin labeling (ASL)-based perfusion imaging is desirable for many applications but suffers from low SNR and motion sensitivity due to the necessity for highly segmented readouts. Acquisition and reconstruction strategies were optimized for motion-robust high-resolution pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (pCASL) of the brain at 3T using segmented 3D Gradient and Spin Echo (3D-GRASE) at 2.0-mm isotropic resolution. Methods: A high-resolution 3D-GRASE pCASL sequence was implemented at 3T and evaluated with a focus on the interaction between background suppression strength and motion-corrected reconstruction, together with the fat suppression and control-tag subtraction strategies that strong suppression requires. Motion correction was performed using a novel motion-compensated (alignedSENSE-based) reconstruction that simultaneously estimates the motion and image, accounting for contrast changes between tag and control data. Eight healthy volunteers were scanned under motion-free and cued motion conditions. Image quality was assessed against motion-free reference images using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and a structural similarity index measure (SSIM). Results: The optimized acquisition-reconstruction pipeline enabled robust 2.0-mm isotropic pCASL at 3T and showed improved resistance to motion-related degradation. Strong BGS provided near-complete suppression of static tissue, and water excitation reduced lipid contamination and improved coil sensitivity estimation. The regularized alignedSENSE motion correction further improved perfusion-image quality, increasing SSIM by 18.7% under Strong BGS. Conclusion: Robust high-resolution pCASL at 3T can be achieved through combined optimization of acquisition and reconstruction. The combination of Strong BGS, water excitation, reference-superimposed processing, and regularized motion correction mitigates motion-related degradation and yields higher-quality perfusion images for high-resolution ASL.

items.title_en: Comparative efficacy and safety of targeted disease-modifying therapies in adults with primary IgA nephropathy: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
items.abstract_en: Background: Targeted disease-modifying therapies for adults with primary IgA nephropathy are increasing in number. However, head-to-head evidence is limited, and trial endpoints and follow-up durations vary. The relative effects of these therapies on short-term proteinuria control, long-term kidney outcomes, and safety remain unclear. Methods: We searched databases and trial registries for randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials with a planned treatment duration of at least 24 weeks alongside stable or optimized supportive care. Frequentist random-effects network meta-analyses evaluated baseline-adjusted geometric mean ratios (GMRs) for 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at 32 to 40 and 24 to 52 weeks, with Holm correction applied. Total estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) slope and composite kidney outcomes were synthesized using common-effect models. Serious adverse events (SAEs) were analyzed using penalized-likelihood logistic regression within risk windows. Sensitivity analyses included restriction to evidence at low risk of bias, exclusion of interim or stage-specific reports, and assessment of precision-recovery assumptions and time-window boundaries. The Mantel to Haenszel method without continuity correction assessed the robustness of sparse SAE results. RoB 2 and CINeMA assessed risk of bias and evidence certainty, respectively. Results: Seventeen trials were included. At 32 to 40 weeks, telitacicept and subcutaneous sibeprenlimab had the lowest GMR point estimates versus placebo: 0.450 (nominal 95% CI 0.323 to 0.628) and 0.488 (0.355 to 0.671), respectively. None of the seven targeted treatment comparisons reached statistical significance after Holm correction. Iptacopan had the largest point estimate for improvement in annualized total eGFR slope: 3.020 mL/min/1.73 m2/year (95% CI 2.025 to 4.015). Composite kidney outcome hazard ratios were 0.570 (95% CI 0.401 to 0.811) for iptacopan and 0.440 (0.271 to 0.714) for targeted-release budesonide. Telitacicept had the lowest SAE odds ratio point estimate at 36 to 39 weeks: 0.314 (95% CI 0.105 to 0.938), although safety estimates were imprecise. In sensitivity analyses, proteinuria effect directions were generally consistent, but the 95% CIs for all retained comparisons included 1 after excluding interim or stage-specific reports; sparse SAE estimates remained imprecise. Evidence certainty was rated as low or very low. Conclusion: Although some regimens yielded the most favorable point estimates, the available evidence remains insufficient to establish treatment priorities or comparative safety advantages. Head-to-head trials are needed.

items.title_en: Distinct neural representations encode psychiatric states across timescales
items.abstract_en: Psychiatric states manifest over multiple timescales, from transient fluctuations in disorder-related distress to long-term variations in disease severity, yet whether these expressions share common neural representations remains unknown. We addressed this question in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) by comparing neural activity associated with momentary distress evoked by triggers versus that associated with clinically assessed chronic symptom severity. We analyzed intracranial recordings from the ventral capsule and orbitofrontal cortex spanning more than 4595 patient-days in 8 individuals undergoing deep brain stimulation therapy (NCT03457675, NCT04281134, NCT04806516), together with quantitative facial- and speech-derived behavioral measures. Neural signatures of OCD severity were dissociable from and stronger than signatures of momentary distress, indicating distinct underlying brain states. Integrating behavioral data into a predictive computational model improved neural decoding performance of both momentary distress and OCD severity. These findings show that acute manifestations of psychiatric illness are not simply short-timescale readouts of the same neural states that encode longer-term clinical burden. Instead, transient distress and longitudinal disease severity are represented by dissociable neural processes. This distinction has important implications for how psychiatric biomarkers and adaptive neuromodulation strategies should be designed.

items.title_en: Beyond reduced alpha power: a weaker temporal link between alpha and other brain rhythms in Alzheimer's disease
items.abstract_en: Background: Reduced alpha power is among the most consistently reported resting electroencephalography (EEG) features of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, alpha activity also interacts with other rhythms over time, a dynamic aspect that power measures do not capture. Whether AD weakens this temporal interaction, and whether such a change carries information beyond reduced alpha power, remains unclear. Methods: We analyzed public eyes-closed resting EEG from 29 healthy controls (HC), 36 patients with AD and 23 with frontotemporal dementia (FTD). After separating periodic from aperiodic activity, we tracked the aperiodic exponent and periodic theta, alpha, beta and gamma activity in consecutive 1-s windows. A vector autoregressive model predicted these five measures from the preceding window. Alpha's predictive contribution (G) was the increase in prediction error for theta, beta and gamma when the model was refitted without alpha as a predictor, with training and testing on separate time blocks of each recording. AD-HC differences were adjusted for age and sex, then for alpha expression (periodic alpha power) and signal quality (dynamic range and spatial reliability), with alpha self-persistence (alpha's carry-over between windows) as a benchmark. We also tested whether expression and G each added information about AD beyond the other. An exploratory Jansen-Rit-family circuit model examined whether expression and G can change partly independently. Results: G was lower in AD than in HC (adjusted difference in 10^3G, -3.19; 95% confidence interval -5.25 to -1.13; p = 0.0035), with a consistent direction across sensitivity analyses. Adjustment for alpha expression and signal quality retained 75.8% of this difference but only 4.4% of the self-persistence difference. Expression and G each added information beyond the other (Holm-adjusted p = 0.012 for both). FTD contrasts were inconclusive. In the circuit model, reducing local recurrent excitation lowered alpha expression without an estimated decrease in G, whereas reducing downstream input lowered G with a smaller change in expression. Conclusions: At the group level, the resting alpha abnormality in AD comprises two partly nonredundant dimensions: reduced expression and a weaker temporal link between alpha and subsequent multi-rhythm activity. Quantifying this temporal link may complement conventional spectral markers of AD.

items.title_en: A family-aware All of Us benchmark for polygenic prediction and genomic machine learning
items.title_zh: 面向多基因预测与基因组机器学习的家族感知All of Us基准
items.abstract_en: Polygenic risk scores (PRSs) have improved substantially in predictive performance, yet results remain difficult to compare across studies that differ in cohorts, phenotype definitions, and evaluation procedures. Comparison to machine-learning methods is harder still, since their performance depends strongly on how data are partitioned and whether related individuals leak across splits. Here, we introduce a family-aware benchmark for polygenic prediction built on version 9 of the All of Us Research Program (AoU). The benchmark assigns entire family components to fixed discovery, calibration, and test partitions, reserves first-degree relatives for within-family evaluation, and separates models trained only on AoU discovery data from those using external GWAS summary statistics. This enables direct comparison between conventional PRS pipelines and machine-learning models trained under identical data budgets. We report results for 14 binary disease traits. Our strongest scores explain 5.7-24.9% of liability-scale variance, with particularly strong prediction for Alzheimer's disease, type 2 diabetes, prostate cancer, glaucoma, and inflammatory bowel disease, and match or exceed published commercial and academic scores for most traits. Across 12 traits with interpretable within-family estimates of within-sibship-to-population effect ratio, 11 confidence intervals included a ratio of 1. Type 2 diabetes showed an attenuation ratio of 0.86 [0.76, 0.97].

items.title_en: Predicting Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis Treatment Outcomes: A Leakage-Controlled Evaluation of Topological Data Analysis Augmentation
items.abstract_en: We asked what topological structure adds to a clinical prediction model and how that addition should be measured. Drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) treatment outcome prediction is the testbed. The contribution is an evaluation design and a bounded null result. Cross-sectional records for 9210 patients from the NIAID TB Portals programme were collated to one row per patient by worst-case aggregation, giving a 99-feature clinical schema. We derived two topological representations. A Mapper graph, built on a UMAP lens over a Gower dissimilarity, supplied four neighbourhood-position features. Local Vietoris--Rips persistent homology on each patient's 26-point neighbourhood supplied degree-0 and degree-1 summaries, vectorised by the best of thirteen catalogued methods. We compared five feature configurations across four classifiers in a pipeline in which every topological step is fitted inside the training partition. A sealed test lockbox of 1776 patients, 463 of them with adverse outcomes, was opened once. We compared discrimination by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) using paired DeLong tests with Bonferroni correction (corrected threshold 0.0125). No topologically augmented configuration meaningfully improved lockbox AUROC over the clinical-only baseline under any classifier. The best AUROC was 0.7548, achieved by the baseline with XGBoost. Across all sixteen comparisons the upper 95% confidence limit never exceeded +0.014 AUROC. Five comparisons met the corrected threshold. Four favoured the baseline, and one, under the support vector machine, favoured the augmented model by a negligible +0.0005 AUROC.The same features supported neighbourhood-based risk stratification and revealed variation in adverse-outcome composition across patient neighbourhoods: adverse-outcome purity ranged from 5.9% to 30.5% across the fifteen largest Mapper nodes, stably under resampling. The findings support a complementary framing of topological data analysis in clinical prediction. Topological features are best understood not as replacements for clinical predictors but as an analytical lens that reveals geometric structure in the patient population not captured by the clinical feature representation alone.

items.title_en: Fibrinolysis resistance in sepsis assessed by serial beside viscoelastometry is associated with plasma protein profiles and organ-failure severity: a prospective observational study
items.abstract_en: Background: Fibrinolysis resistance is associated with adverse outcomes in sepsis and can be quantified at the bedside by tissue plasminogen activator-enhanced viscoelastometric testing, using the fibrin-adjusted (FIBA10) clot lysis time (TPA-LT) expressed as the TPA-LT/FIBA10 ratio. In this study of adults admitted to intensive care with sepsis, plasma tissue plasminogen activator activity, plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 activity (PAI-1), plasminogen and a2-antiplasmin were measured serially alongside TPA-LT/FIBA10 and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA-2) scores. Whether the bedside TPA-LT/FIBA10 measure of fibrinolysis resistance reflects the underlying plasma fibrinolytic protein environment, and whether it tracks organ-failure severity, has not been established. Results: This prospective observational study included 283 paired observations in 69 septic patients admitted with a median Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation III score 81, median SOFA-2 score 13 and a 38% ICU mortality. PAI-1 increased and plasminogen decreased with increasing fibrinolysis resistance (1.77 [1.50-2.09]-fold increase and 0.81 [0.76-0.87]-fold decrease, respectively, per e-fold increase in TPA-LT/FIBA10). Increasing organ-failure severity was also associated with increased PAI-1 and decreased plasminogen (1.23 [1.17-1.29]-fold increase and 0.95 [0.93-0.96]-fold decrease, respectively, per point increase in SOFA-2). In contrast, tissue plasminogen activator activity and absolute a2-antiplasmin did not relate to fibrinolysis resistance or organ failure. Principal component analysis of the fibrinolysis proteins, organ-failure severity and fibrinolysis resistance identified a dominant axis explaining 35% of the variance, on which PAI-1, SOFA-2 and TPA-LT/FIBA10 loaded together in opposition to plasminogen. Unsupervised clustering of the dataset, performed without reference to patient outcomes, separated a fibrinolysis inhibitor- high, substrate-depleted group with 61% mortality compared to 29% in the preserved- fibrinolysis group. During the ICU stay, PAI-1 decreased within 72 hours in survivors but remained unchanged in non-survivors (interaction p<0.001). A trend was observed for plasminogen levels increasing in survivors but remaining static in non-survivors. Conclusions: Changes in key fibrinolysis proteins, organ-failure severity and fibrinolysis resistance measured by viscoelastometry were coupled facets of the response to sepsis dominated by fibrinolysis inhibitor excess and substrate depletion rather than by reduced activator availability. These findings provide biological validation for bedside viscoelastometric quantification of fibrinolysis resistance and support prospective evaluation of substrate-directed profibrinolytic strategies.

items.title_en: Interventions for Cognitive Impairment in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: An Umbrella Review of Pharmacological and Lifestyle Strategies, Mechanisms, and Clinical Implications
items.abstract_en: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is one of the fastest-growing epidemics associated with cognitive impairment and dementia. This reduces quality of life among patients with diabetes. Several trials on the management of cognitive impairment have been conducted, although their effectiveness and mechanisms are still unclear. Aim: To synthesize evidence from systematic reviews and meta-analyses of RCTs examining interventions for cognitive impairment in T2DM, stratified by intervention category, comparator, patient characteristics, mechanisms, and clinical outcomes. Methods: We identified 11 systematic reviews (n = 213,604 participants) reporting the effects of cognitive impairment interventions through a comprehensive literature search. Using random-effects models, a meta-meta-analysis was conducted and heterogeneity assessed using I{superscript 2} statistics. AMSTAR and GRADE were used to assess the quality of reviews. Subgroup analyses were conducted for intervention category, cognitive severity, age, diabetes duration, sex, and follow-up duration. Results: Sodium glucose co-transporter inhibitors showed the strongest cognitive improvement effect (pooled OR = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.35-0.55; SUCRA = 94.5%), followed by GLP-1 receptor agonists (RR/OR = 0.60, 95% CI: 0.50-0.72; SUCRA = 92.1%). Among lifestyle interventions, multi-component exercise was the most effective (SMD = 0.69-1.04). The lower baseline cognition (MMSE < 23) benefited more from GLP-1 receptor agonists (Cohen's d = -3.00, p < 0.001). Advanced age ([≥]60 years) and prolonged intervention time ([≥]24 weeks for medications; [≥]6 months for exercise) were associated with greater effects. Female gender showed greater benefit from GLP-1 receptor agonists (HR = 0.63 vs 0.81 for male gender). Conclusions: SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists have the greatest effect on cognition in T2DM, and multi-component exercise is the most effective lifestyle component. The review therefore recommends individualized selection of interventions based on patient characteristics and baseline cognitive status. This calls for high-quality trials with prolonged follow-up to strengthen the evidence base.

items.title_en: Association between Blood Lead Levels and Anaemia in a Pregnant Population in the Kintampo Area of Ghana: A Prospective Cohort Study
items.abstract_en: Background: Maternal anaemia and lead exposure both pose substantial risks in pregnancy, but their relationship has not been consistently explored. We assessed trimester-specific blood lead levels (BLLs) and their association with anaemia in pregnant women in the Kintampo area of Ghana. Methods: In this prospective cohort study nested within the PRISMA Maternal and Newborn Health Study in Ghana, 300 pregnant women were enrolled at <14 weeks' gestation and followed until delivery. Trimester-specific venous blood was collected and analysed for haemoglobin levels using Sysmex XN 330 auto analyser (Sysmex Corporation, Japan) and BLL using inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Anaemia was defined as 11.0g/dL for first (T1) and third (T3) trimesters and 10.5g/dL for second (T2) trimester according to the World Health Organisation's (WHO's) trimester-specific haemoglobin thresholds and elevated BLL as [≥]3.5 {micro}g/dL by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Multiple logistic regression, adjusted for maternal age, parity, education, malaria parasitaemia, body mass index, gestational age and occupation, examined the BLL and anaemia association. A population-averaged Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) model was used to assess the association between elevated BLL and anaemia across trimesters. Results: The mean age of participants was 27.7{+/-}5.8 years (range 18-44years). Geometric mean BLL increased significantly across trimesters from 1.0 to 1.3 to 1.5 {micro}g/dL (p=0.003) for T1, T2 and T3 respectively. The prevalence of elevated BLL ([≥]3.5 {micro}g/dL) was 10.7%, 7.6%, and 15.2% for T1, T2, and T3 respectively. Anaemia prevalence increased significantly with increasing trimester from 34.7.0% to 59.3% to 76.0% (p<0.001) for T1, T2 and T3 respectively. In the population-averaged GEE model, elevated BLL was associated with increased odds of anaemia across trimesters, though this did not reach statistical significance (OR = 1.29, 95% CI: 0.77-2.17, p = 0.327). Conclusion: Anaemia prevalence in pregnancy is high in the Kintampo area and increases with advancing gestation. No significant association was observed between BLL and anaemia. These findings reinforce anaemia as a priority for urgent interventions in pregnancy through pathways independent of lead exposure. However, occupational lead surveillance and control remain important policy considerations.

items.title_en: Complete entropy contraction from conditional hyperboundedness
items.title_zh: 由条件超有界性得到完全熵收缩
items.abstract_en: For finite-dimensional quantum channels compatible with a faithful conditional expectation, we show that conditional hyperboundedness and strict GNS contraction together yield a relative entropy contraction. For KMS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups, a conditional $2\to q$ hyperboundedness at time $t_0>0$ combined with a GNS gap $λ>0$ implies a modified logarithmic Sobolev constant \[ α=\frac{λ(1-2/q)} {12(λt_0+\log M+1-2/q)},\] where $M$ is the hyperboundedness constant. As a consequence, completely bounded hyperboundedness over auxiliary systems gives complete versions of entropy contraction with the same rates.
items.abstract_zh: 对于与忠实条件期望相容的有限维量子信道，作者证明条件超有界性与严格 GNS 收缩共同推出相对熵收缩。对于 KMS 对称量子马尔可夫半群，在某个 t0>0 时刻的条件 2→q 超有界性，结合 GNS 间隙 λ>0，可推出修正对数 Sobolev 常数 α = λ(1-2/q) / [12(λt0+log M+1-2/q)]，其中 M 为超有界性常数。由此，在辅助系统上的完全有界超有界性可给出具有相同速率的完全版熵收缩。
items.highlight_zh: 条件超有界性加严格 GNS 收缩推出相对熵收缩
items.digest_zh: 这篇论文属于量子信息与算子代数交叉领域，研究量子信道和量子马尔可夫半群的熵收缩问题。相对熵收缩描述的是：经过信道或时间演化后，两个量子态之间的相对熵下降速度有多快，它与修正对数 Sobolev 不等式和混合时间密切相关。作者考虑有限维量子信道，并要求其与一个忠实的条件期望相容。核心结论是：条件超有界性加上严格的 GNS 收缩，可以推出相对熵收缩。对于 KMS 对称的量子马尔可夫半群，作者进一步给出定量版本：若在某个正时刻 t0 具有条件 2→q 超有界性，且存在 GNS 间隙 λ，则得到显式的修正对数 Sobolev 常数 α，其表达式同时依赖 λ、t0、超有界性常数 M 和 q。更重要的是，把超有界性提升到辅助系统上的完全有界版本后，可得到完全熵收缩，并保持相同速率。该结果把函数不等式式的条件与量子信道的熵 contraction 联系起来，为研究量子半群的完全混合与稳定性提供了统一工具。

items.title_en: Network nonlocality with tripartite entangled sources
items.title_zh: 三方纠缠源下的网络非局域性
items.abstract_en: Quantum networks are built from independent sources, and their nonlocality has mostly been studied with sources that emit bipartite entangled states. A source of three entangled qubits is richer, since its nonlocality can be tested by the Mermin or the more demanding Svetlichny inequality. We ask how network nonlocality relates to these two single-source notions and find that the answer depends on the wiring. When two central nodes without inputs share every source, Bell-state measurements turn every Svetlichny violation into a network violation, and even all entangled generalised Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger states violate the network inequality. When a single central node is shared, the relation reverses, and a network violation requires a Mermin violation of the source. With more sources, the maximal violation depends on whether their number is even or odd, and we give tight bounds for both cases. These results show that the way multipartite sources are wired decides which kind of nonlocality a network inherits.
items.abstract_zh: 量子网络由相互独立的源构建，其非局域性此前多基于发射两体纠缠态的源来研究。能发射三个纠缠量子比特的源更为丰富，其非局域性可由 Mermin 不等式或要求更高的 Svetlichny 不等式检验。我们考察网络非局域性与这两种单源非局域性概念之间的关系，发现答案取决于源的连接方式。当两个无输入的中心节点共享每一个源时，Bell 态测量会把任何 Svetlichny 违背转化为网络违背，甚至所有纠缠的广义 Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger 态都会违背网络不等式。当仅共享一个中心节点时，关系反转，网络违背要求源存在 Mermin 违背。源更多时，最大违背取决于源数目为奇数还是偶数，我们给出两种情形的紧致界。这些结果表明，多体源的接线方式决定网络继承哪一类非局域性。
items.highlight_zh: 源的接线方式决定网络继承哪一类非局域性
items.digest_zh:
1) 研究问题：量子网络由多个独立纠缠源和若干节点组成，节点之间互不通信，只共享纠缠。以往研究网络非局域性时，多假设每个源只发出两体纠缠态；若源本身发出三量子比特纠缠（GHZ 类），它能展现 Mermin 非局域性，甚至更强的 Svetlichny 非局域性。那么，这种“单个源内部的非局域性”与整个网络的非局域性究竟是什么关系？
2) 方法：作者在理论上构造网络贝尔实验，比较两种典型接线：一是两个没有输入的“中心”节点共享全部源；二是只共享一个中心节点。节点内部采用 Bell 态测量作为联合测量，分析在什么条件下网络不等式被违背，并推导最大违背量。
3) 结果：关系取决于接线方式。两中心共享每个源时，任何 Svetlichny 违背都会转化为网络违背，连所有纠缠的广义 GHZ 态都能违背网络不等式；只共享一个中心节点时关系反转，网络违背反而要求源违背 Mermin 不等式。当源数目更多时，最大违背依赖于源数是奇还是偶，作者对两种情形都给出了紧致的界。
4) 意义：这说明多体纠缠源的“拓扑接线”决定了网络能否把源的量子性转化为可观测的非局域关联，为网络量子信息实验的设计与判据选择提供了明确指引。

items.title_en: Interference-induced dynamical crossovers in quantum walks on disordered square lattices
items.title_zh: 无序方格子上量子行走中干涉诱导的动力学交叉
items.abstract_en: We study discrete-time quantum walks with Fourier, Grover, and Hadamard coin operators on disordered square lattices, alongside classical random walks. Edges in the lattice are absent with a probability, $p$. In this case, both classical and quantum walks exhibit an essentially identical degradation of transport. We then study a general version of this model, in which the existing edges are retained. However, the absent edges are no longer absent, but now become partially transmitting, with a transmission coefficient $f$. We find that the response is now quite sensitive to the walk protocol and coin symmetry. The classical walk exhibits asymptotic stability of the anomalous diffusion exponent, $β(t)$. In comparison, quantum walks exhibit a monotonically decaying $β(t)$ beyond the initial transient regime, leading to the absence of quantum diffusion in two dimensions. We map the transport regimes in the $(f,p)$ plane and identify the contour for $β=1$, which separates the subdiffusive and superdiffusive regimes. We also examine the effective diffusion coefficient, the inverse participation ratio, and the first two moments of edge transmission. We restrict ourselves to analyzing bulk propagation prior to finite-size boundary reflections. The results indicate that quantum transport depends significantly on coin-specific interference and cannot be fully described by transmission statistics alone.
items.abstract_zh: 我们研究 Fourier、Grover 与 Hadamard 硬币算符在无序方格子上实现的离散时间量子行走，并与经典随机行走对照。格子的边以概率 p 缺失，此时经典与量子行走的输运退化几乎相同。随后研究该模型的一般化版本：保留已有的边，但缺失的边不再完全消失，而是变为部分透射，透射系数为 f。我们发现响应此时对行走协议与硬币对称性相当敏感。经典行走的异常扩散指数 β(t) 具有渐近稳定性；相比之下，量子行走在初始瞬态之后 β(t) 单调衰减，导致二维中量子扩散消失。我们绘制了 (f,p) 平面的输运相图，并确定了 β=1 的等值线，用以划分亚扩散与超扩散区域；还考察了有效扩散系数、逆参与比以及边透射的前两阶矩。分析限于有限尺寸边界反射发生之前的体传播。结果表明，量子输运显著依赖硬币特有的干涉，无法仅由透射统计完全描述。
items.highlight_zh: 量子行走输运由硬币相关干涉主导，无法仅用透射统计刻画
items.digest_zh:
1) 研究问题：当介质存在缺陷或断边时，粒子如何扩散？量子行走中的相干干涉与经典随机行走的随机扩散本质不同，作者想弄清在方格子上同时引入“断边”和“弱透射”时，量子输运与经典输运会如何分化。
2) 方法：采用离散时间量子行走，分别使用 Fourier、Grover、Hadamard 三种硬币算符，并在方格子上让每条边以概率 p 缺失；随后推广模型，使“缺失”的边变为以系数 f 部分透射的边。作者将量子结果与经典随机行走对照，测量异常扩散指数 β(t)、有效扩散系数、逆参与比以及边透射的前两阶矩，并只关注边界反射到达之前的体传播。
3) 结果：当边完全缺失（f=0）时，量子与经典行走的输运退化几乎一模一样；一旦存在部分透射，响应就强烈依赖行走协议和硬币的对称性。经典行走的扩散指数 β 在长时间下趋于稳定，而量子行走的 β 在初始瞬态后单调下降，导致二维中量子扩散消失。作者绘制了 (f,p) 平面的输运相图，用 β=1 的等值线分隔亚扩散与超扩散区。
4) 意义：说明量子输运不能只用“有多少边能透射”这类统计量描述，硬币带来的干涉结构才是关键；这对理解无序环境中的量子传输与局域化、设计量子输运器件有参考价值。

items.title_en: Sparse Carleman Embeddings for Nonlinear Discrete Dynamical Systems
items.title_zh: 非线性离散动力系统的稀疏Carleman嵌入
items.abstract_en: Discrete nonlinear dynamical systems arise in population models, iterative optimization, and numerical simulations, where computing many iterations can be costly in high dimensions. We study Carleman embedding for forced quadratic discrete systems and its application to quantum state preparation. Under explicit stability and initial-state assumptions, we prove that the truncation error decreases geometrically with the embedding degree, uniformly over all iterations. A central obstacle in discrete time is that the lifted update can become dense even when the original coefficient maps are sparse. We overcome this obstacle by constructing an exact auxiliary linear-system representation that applies the coefficient maps one tensor factor at a time, with row and column sparsities bounded independently of the truncation degree. After rescaling, the associated history system has a condition number that grows linearly with the iteration count, uniformly in the truncation degree. These results yield a quantum algorithm for preparing an approximation to the normalized $n$th iterate with constant success probability. Under coherent input-access assumptions, and for fixed sparsity, stability parameters, and a known positive lower bound on the final-state norm, the oracle query complexity is linear in $n$ and polylogarithmic in the inverse accuracy. Numerical experiments in one and three dimensions illustrate the convergence of the truncated embedding.

items.title_en: The $\varepsilon$-smoothed Entanglement of Formation and its relation to the Moreau-Yosida approximation
items.title_zh: ε-平滑形成纠缠及其与Moreau-Yosida逼近的关系
items.abstract_en: We describe a family of convex continuous functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, on the set of states of a bipartite quantum system (consisting of finite-dimensional or infinite-dimensional subsystems) obtained by applying the Mora-Piani-Briegel construction of $\varepsilon$-measure (proposed in [Phys. Rev. A 109, 052413]) to the Entanglement of Formation (EoF) with the use of the trace norm distance in the role of basic metric. These functions are non-increasing in $\varepsilon$ and converge pointwise to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$. We conducted a detailed analysis of properties of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, using (among others) the relationship between the family $\{E_{F,\varepsilon}\}_{\varepsilon\in[0,1]}$ and the family $\{E^λ_F(ρ)\}_{λ>0}$ of Moreau-Yosida approximations of the EoF explored in [arXiv:2609.30246]. We obtain a variational expression for the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ (which for $\varepsilon=0$ turns into the standard variational expression for the EoF). We also describe the weak subadditivity property of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ and analyse their continuity properties. The semicontinuity bounds for the EoF (presented in [Lob.J.Math., 46, 2632-2658],[arXiv:2404.07978]) allow us to obtain easily computable upper bounds on the rate of uniform convergence of the function $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ on the sets of states with bounded rank/energy of one of the marginal states. Applicability of the obtained results to other entanglement measures, in particular, to the relative entropy of entanglement, is discussed. As an auxiliary result, it is shown that for any state of an infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system, there exists a nearest separable state w.r.t. the trace norm distance. The non-uniqueness of such a state is also shown.

items.title_en: Tapering to Enhance the Performance of Nanowire-Based Fluorescent Biosensors
items.title_zh: 锥化结构提升纳米线荧光生物传感器性能
items.abstract_en: High-refractive-index nanowires are of interest for signal enhancement in fluorescence-based biosensing. Here, through electromagnetic modelling, we demonstrate substantial fluorescence signal enhancement by incorporating a tapered section into a cylindrical nanowire and investigate two complementary tapering configurations to address practical implementation challenges. Under near-normal excitation, the excitation enhancement increases approximately linearly with taper length, reaching more than three times that of the corresponding non-tapered nanowire at a taper length of 8000 nm. In a non-imaging signal detection scheme using a low numerical aperture (NA), the proposed tapered nanowire achieves more than three orders of magnitude enhancement in fluorescence signal compared with a planar biosensor. Thus, the tapered nanowire should enable efficient fluorescence detection using compact, low-NA optical configuration. In imaging mode, similarly as for non-tapered nanowires, imaging sharpness beyond conventional microscopy limitations is obtained when imaging from the non-tapered nanowire end, while strongly increased excitation enhancement is simultaneously obtained when exciting from the opposite, tapered end.
items.abstract_zh: 高折射率纳米线在荧光生物传感的信号增强方面颇具价值。本文通过电磁建模证明，在圆柱形纳米线中引入锥形段可显著增强荧光信号，并研究了两种互补的锥化构型以应对实际实现中的挑战。在近垂直激发下，激发增强随锥长近似线性增长，锥长为 8000 nm 时可达对应无锥纳米线的三倍以上。在采用低数值孔径（NA）的非成像信号探测方案中，所提出的锥化纳米线相比平面生物传感器实现了三个数量级以上的荧光信号增强，因而可用紧凑的低 NA 光学配置实现高效荧光检测。在成像模式下，与非锥化纳米线类似，从非锥化端成像可获得超越常规显微镜极限的成像锐度，同时从相对的锥化端激发又能大幅提高激发增强。
items.highlight_zh: 锥形纳米线令低NA光学系统荧光信号增强超千倍
items.digest_zh:
1) 研究问题：荧光生物传感靠微弱的光信号识别分子，如何在不使用昂贵大数值孔径（NA）物镜的前提下把信号放大，是实用化的关键。高折射率纳米线能增强局域电场并改善荧光收集，但如何设计才能兼顾激发与探测？
2) 方法：作者用电磁建模（数值仿真）研究圆柱形纳米线，并在其一端加入锥形过渡段，比较两种互补的锥化方案，以应对加工与对准上的现实困难。评估指标包括近垂直激发下的激发增强倍数、低 NA 非成像探测下的总荧光信号，以及成像模式下的分辨率与激发增强的权衡。
3) 结果：激发增强随锥长近似线性上升，锥长 8000 nm 时超过无锥纳米线的 3 倍；在低 NA 探测方案中，相比平面传感器荧光信号提升三个数量级以上，意味着用紧凑、低成本的光学系统即可高效检测。成像模式下，从非锥端成像仍能获得超越常规显微极限的锐度，而从锥端激发又能同时获得很高的激发增强。
4) 意义：该设计把“看得清”和“激得亮”分别分配给纳米线的两端，降低了对光学系统的要求，为低成本、易集成的荧光生物传感器提供了可行路径。

items.title_en: Twist-controlled imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems
items.title_zh: 量子自旋系统中扭转控制的虚时间Mpemba效应
items.abstract_en: We construct a controllable imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems using spatially modulated local rotations without changing initial bipartite entanglement spectra and correlation magnitudes. This feature unambiguously isolates the redistribution of spectral weights as the sole driver of the anomalous relaxation. Using the compact-boson description, we reveal that these twists act as precise mode selectors: higher-harmonic twists exclusively populate high-energy standing waves, structurally bypassing slow-decaying infrared modes to accelerate convergence. We derive exact analytical crossing times for these reversals and demonstrate that intentionally reintroducing the slow-mode population systematically delays the ITME. This exact mechanism is validated beyond the fixed-point theory via calculations on interacting XXZ chains and ladders. Furthermore, a twelve-qubit simulation of variational quantum imaginary-time evolution reproduces the reversals and their controlled delay, providing a concrete route to realize this protocol in realistic quantum circuits. Ultimately, these results provide a strictly controllable and exact starting point for realizing and investigating the imaginary-time Mpemba effect, establishing a foundational paradigm to harness anomalous non-equilibrium relaxation in quantum ground-state preparations.

items.title_en: Growth Phase Map of α and \b{eta} Tantalum as a Function of Growth Temperature and Oxygen Partial Pressure
items.title_zh: α和β钽的生长相图：生长温度与氧分压的函数关系
items.abstract_en: Tantalum thin films are used in low-loss superconducting quantum circuits, yet the growth conditions governing selection of $α$-Ta(110), $α$-Ta(111), and metastable $β$-Ta on c-plane sapphire remain uncertain. We deposited 100 nm Ta films by dc magnetron sputtering on Al$_2$O$_3$(0001) at 300-900 $^\circ$C while varying the O$_2$ partial pressure from a $5.5\times10^{-11}$ Torr ultrahigh-vacuum baseline to $2.23\times10^{-4}$ Torr. Absorption-corrected X-ray diffraction texture coefficients were used to construct a ternary phase-orientation growth map in terms of temperature and the oxygen-to-Ta impingement flux ratio ($2Φ_{O_2}/Φ_{Ta}\leq4.8\times10^{-6}$ to 19). Without added oxygen, $α$-Ta(110) dominated at every temperature. At an O$_2$ pressure of only $2.5\times10^{-9}$ Torr ($2Φ_{O_2}/Φ_{Ta}=2.2\times10^{-4}$), $α$-Ta(111) accounted for 98-99% of the normalized texture weight from 300 to 700 $^\circ$C, decreasing to 65% at 900 $^\circ$C. Substantial $β$-Ta formed only at the highest oxygen dose, dominating at 300 $^\circ$C and disappearing at 900 $^\circ$C. The apparent $β$(001)/$α$(110) selection energy of $1.07\pm0.16$ eV is comparable to the activation energy for oxygen diffusion in Ta, consistent with oxygen transport influencing phase selection. Oxygen also produced orientation-dependent changes in crystallite size and microstrain. These findings establish oxygen-controlled processing windows for phase- and orientation-selective growth of Ta films for superconducting devices.

items.title_en: Compositional Operational Rank, Smooth Realizability, and Dimensional Reduction
items.title_zh: 组合操作秩、光滑可实现性与降维
items.abstract_en: Higher-dimensional theories distinguish the dimensionality of a microscopic description from the number of directions accessible to a physical observer. Relating these notions requires not only dimensional reduction, but also a consistent preservation of operational independence across different levels of description. We establish sufficient conditions under which a compositional operational rank is preserved first as the dimension of a smooth integral leaf and then as an observable Fisher-information rank. The key requirement is closure-faithfulness: the smooth realization must preserve the dependency relations of the operational closure, rather than merely its total rank. Together with real representability, constant rank, involutivity, and observer/scale compatibility, this yields a local integral leaf whose dimension equals the operational rank. A further primary-identification condition is required at the measurement level. If an independently specified observer image coincides locally with the primary integral distribution and the admissible protocols provide local resolution, finite labeled-mixture closure, and locally constant outcome support, then the same rank can be realized by a finite composite Fisher-information protocol. The construction holds for arbitrary finite rank. At r = 4 it provides a conditional operational criterion for dimensional reduction in higher-dimensional theories: a viable reduction must preserve the relevant operational dependency structure, not merely produce four effective coordinates. Quantum-hardware negative controls further show that the same restricted Fisher rank can conceal different larger ranks under a broader pre-specified measurement protocol. The framework therefore constrains the operational outcome of dimensional reduction without imposing a universal four-dimensional bound on microscopic state spaces.

items.title_en: Competing coherence geometries in positive maps: positivity hierarchies, atomicity, and optimal entanglement witnesses
items.title_zh: 正映射中的竞争相干几何：正性层级、原子性与最优纠缠见证
items.abstract_en: We introduce a family of positive maps on qudits whose Choi operators combine two competing coherence patterns: independent exchange couplings and a collective set of diagonal couplings. For every mixed member of the family, we derive exact conditions for positivity, complete positivity, and all intermediate levels of k-positivity, and we determine the complete phase structure of decomposability and atomicity. The higher-positivity thresholds depend on the channel multiplicities, whereas the exact decomposability boundary is universal in scale-free coordinates. Its proof combines an explicit positive-plus-copositive decomposition with a matching family of positive-partial-transpose (PPT) states. The latter form PPT edge states whose detection region is an ellipse, or a disk after collective rescaling. An embedded-qutrit certificate shows that indecomposability and atomicity coincide throughout the mixed family. In contrast, the purely collective endpoint is decomposable over its entire positive interval. Finally, at maximal coherence, an explicit positive subtraction produces an atomic optimal entanglement witness with the spanning property and a strictly larger PPT- detection set. The study thus provides an exactly solvable setting in which k-positivity, decomposability, atomicity, PPT-edge-state geometry, and witness optimality can be compared in arbitrary local dimension.

items.title_en: Daylight-Referenced Efficiency (DRE): A Radiometric Measure of Electric Light Source Efficiency
items.title_zh: 日光参考效率（DRE）：电光源效率的辐射度量方法
items.abstract_en: Photopic luminous efficacy (lm/W) weights optical power strictly against human eye sensitivity V (lambda), creating a systemic metrological penalty for electric light sources engineered with broad spectral output in the ultraviolet (280-380 nm) or infrared (780-4000 nm) bands. Similarly, metrics evaluating chromaticity, color quality, or melanopic pathways assess photoreceptor responses strictly within the visual band, offering no measure of broad-spectrum physical radiant power conversion. To resolve this limitation, we introduce Daylight-Referenced Efficiency (eta_DRE), a radiometric framework that evaluates how efficiently an electric light source converts electrical power into an optical spectrum matching natural terrestrial daylight across domain Omega = [280 nm, 4000 nm]. The framework factorizes performance into primary physical quantities: domain-restricted Wall-Plug Efficiency (eta_wall [W_optical/W_elec]), measuring unweighted electrical-to-optical conversion, and Daylight Spectral Fidelity (eta_spec [unitless, 0-1]), quantifying geometric shape match to the ASTM G173 AM1.5G solar reference via total variation distance (1 - TVD). Multiplying total optical power by spectral fidelity yields the absolute Daylight-Referenced Output Power (P_dr [W]), establishing a direct physical flux quantity for lighting specification. Dividing by electrical drive power gives the summary metric Daylight-Referenced Efficiency (eta_DRE = eta_wall * eta_spec [W/W_elec]), measuring net reference-conforming radiant output per electrical Watt consumed. The mathematical architecture is reference-agnostic, domain-extensible, and maintains provable lower-bound monotonicity for eta_wall and eta_DRE under spectral truncation. Open-source reference software is provided to facilitate deployment and standardized rating of broad-spectrum light sources.

items.title_en: Decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification for quantum low-density parity-check codes
items.title_zh: 量子低密度奇偶校验码的交替加权图稀疏化解码
items.abstract_en: Real-time decoding is a fundamental necessity for building fault-tolerant quantum computers. In this work, we introduce decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification (DAWG), an ensemble based approach that combines Tanner graph sparsification with ensembling belief-propagation (BP) decoders. The DAWG decoder runs BP decoders over the full detector error model Tanner graph for certain iterations to then transfer the posteriors to a sparsified graph in which additional rounds of BP are run. Each of the decoders in the ensemble uses a different transfer matrix to map the posterior information to the sparsified graph. We use the serial schedule for the minimum-sum BP decoders and, thus, employ Vibe decoding ideas by randomizing the schedules of each of them. The performance of the DAWG decoder is then numerically studied for bivariate bicycle codes and superdense color code circuits to be compared with other state-of-the-art decoding approaches. Importantly, the DAWG decoder shows a similar performance to Relay belief-propagation and Vibe decoding when combined with an order-$0$ Localized Statistics Decoding (LSD-$0$) post-processor. Crucially, the post-processor is called an order of magnitude less times than for Vibe with the same ensemble size, indicating that the introduced latency tail will be minimal.
